_doc: flag_days (effects, WEATHER-006, int >= 1, needs set_flag): the flags it sets expire after that many days (read through Effects.flag_active). Random events when exploring. rest_days (top level, ENC-010, int >= 0, default 0; optional per encounter, 0 = never rests): a happening that fades (not repeatable, not a fight) is not eligible until that many days have passed since it was last met. sense_below_chance (top level, ENC-009, 0..1, default 0.2): a NON-lethal foe met while exploring whose win chance is below this is sensed first like a Dangerous lethal foe, so the player chooses to fight or slip away instead of being forced. An encounter is eligible if it shares a tag with the place's tags, the player's realm is within min_realm/max_realm (realm ids, optional; min_stage (optional, ENC-002, needs min_realm): the encounter is only eligible at or above that stage of min_realm (0-based: Qi Refining 3 = the 4th Layer); a player in a higher realm always qualifies), and blocked_by_flag (optional) is unset. rogue_only (optional, C-249, bool, default false): only eligible while the player has no sect. sect_only (optional, C-269, bool, default false): only eligible while the player belongs to a sect (both true is invalid). min_alignment/max_alignment (optional, inclusive, W-004f): only eligible within that alignment range (e.g. righteous enforcers only hunt the wicked). weight is relative; 'kind' fortune/misfortune weights are scaled by the Fortune attribute. effects use the shared effect keys (src/core/systems/effects.gd) and are applied when the encounter happens. enemy (an id in data/enemies.json) starts a fight after the text, unless it is lethal and Deadly for the player, who then senses it and slips away. days = time spent. only_if_applicable: the encounter is only eligible when its effects can apply (e.g. a doctor only finds the injured). weather (optional, ENC-013): list of clear/cloudy/rain/snow/fog; the encounter is only eligible while Weather.of for the region being explored is one of them (ignored on the road). rest_days set on a repeatable or fight encounter also makes it rest that many days (ENC-013); without it those never rest. seasons (optional, SEASON-001): list of spring/summer/autumn/winter; the encounter is only eligible in those seasons (absent = all year). requires_flag (optional): only eligible once that world flag is set (follow-up encounters). choices (optional, W-004c, at least 2; the encounter itself then has no enemy): after the text and effects the player picks one of [{label, text, effects, days, enemy, requires: {min_realm, min_alignment, max_alignment, flag, min_attributes: {attribute id: int >= 1, e.g. {"comprehension": 12}, min_profession: {profession id: rank int 0..max rank (0 = merely practises it), e.g. {"doctor": 1}}}}]; choices() also returns a `check` tag naming the attribute, profession, alignment tier and item cost it needs (CHOICE-003); a choice is disabled when its requires fail or its effects cannot be paid; a chosen enemy is always fought (never evaded). Set flags in a choice's effects (set_flag) to unlock follow-ups. rival (optional, RIV-002): any | stronger | equal | weaker; the encounter needs the player's living rival, whose major realm compares that way to the player's; rival_attitude (optional, RIVAL-010; needs rival): friendly | bitter | proud, or an array of them (RIVAL-022), the encounter only rolls while Rivals.attitude (karma.json rival friendly_favor / bitter_grudge) matches; its text and choice labels/texts may use {rival} and {rival_realm}. With a rival condition, the encounter and each choice may also set rival_grudge (grudge points the rival gains), rival_favor (favor change) and fight_rival (true: a non-lethal fight with the rival, instead of an enemy; with spar: true on the choice it is a friendly spar, RIVAL-022). grateful_npc (optional on a choice, RIV-001f): {amount (gratitude owed), realm (realm id, default mortal), age_years [min, max], gender (optional), favor (optional starting favor)}: choosing it spawns the person helped as an NPC living in the current region who owes the player `amount` gratitude (karma.json); with an enemy, only if the fight is won. {villager} / {elder} (ENC-011, optional in text, choice label/text and on_fail text): a living generated adult of the current region (not family, not the rival; half the time someone the player already knows) and the oldest such person, chosen when the encounter is rolled; an encounter that uses them is ineligible where nobody lives (and on the road). effects may also carry villager_favor / elder_favor (int -20..20, non-zero; needs the placeholder in the texts): favor change with that person. effects may also carry renown (ENC-006, int 1..50): local renown in the current region when the encounter or choice happens. effects may also carry contribution (EFF-001, int 1..500): sect contribution for a sect member (a rogue gets nothing). renown (optional on a choice, RENOWN-004, int 1..50): local renown gained in the current region when the choice is taken; with an enemy, only if the fight is won. check (optional on a choice, ENC-008): {attribute: attribute id, target: number > 0}; the choice succeeds with chance clamp(attribute / target, 0.1, 0.9), rolled on the game rng, and then applies as usual; otherwise its required on_fail block (same keys as the choice's outcome: text, effects, days, enemy, rival_grudge...) applies instead. choices() reports the chance (shown like fight odds). on_fail is only allowed with a check. discovery_only (optional, TRAV-005): true = never rolls at random; it is only the `discovery` of a region in regions.json (shown on the first exploration there). repeatable (optional, ENC-003): true = never fades; ordinary encounters become less likely the more often they have been met (Exploration.freshness), plain gathering ones stay repeatable. min_explores (optional, EXPL-001, int >= 1): only eligible once the player has explored the current region at least that many days (CharacterData.explore_days); never eligible where no region is known. min_renown (optional, RENOWN-002, int tier index into regions.json renown.tiers: 0 Known, 1 Respected, 2 Renowned; the lowest, untitled tier needs no gate): only eligible while the player's renown tier in the region being explored is at least that; never eligible where no region is known; region_progress ignores it for the unrenowned. name (optional): a display title, used for the Discovery: <name> window title (default: the id, prettified).

encounters.text: You wander for a day. Nothing of note happens.
You wander for a day. Nothing of note happens.
After weeks in the mist you notice the same crooked pine twice, and follow the stream behind it into a hidden valley where a small spirit spring wells up among the herbs.

The mist parts on the hidden valley again, and the spring-spirit that dwells there, grown pale and old, waits by the crooked pine. "The roots of this valley are failing," it whispers, pressing a warm seed into your palm. "Carry it to the cliffs of the Azure Peak, where the wind is clean. Or keep it, if your need is greater than mine."

choices.label: Plant it on the Azure Peak cliffs
choices.text: You climb the windswept cliffs and set the seed in a crack of stone, shielding it until a green thread breaks the rock. Somewhere far below, the old spirit sighs in thanks, and the qi of the cliffs grows richer around the new green thread.

choices.label: Swallow the seed yourself
choices.text: The seed melts on your tongue into a rush of spring-water qi that settles hard against your dantian. The valley behind you dims, and the old spirit does not call after you.

encounters.name: The Snapped Axle
encounters.text: A hunter's cart sits canted on the lane with its axle snapped clean through, a load of boar hides spilling into the dust. The hunter squats beside it, turning a chipped skinning blade over and over, and looks at you without much hope.

choices.label: Help him heave the cart aside
choices.text: You put your shoulder to the wheel and drag the cart out of the lane. He thanks you with a handful of coppers' worth of stones and goes off to find a smith.

choices.label: Pick over the spilled hides while he is distracted
choices.text: A few hides vanish under your robe before he looks up. He does not notice, but a neighbour at a window does.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: It is not your cart. The hunter's sigh follows you down the lane.

choices.label: Forge a new axle pin and true the blade
choices.text: You borrow a hearth, draw the iron out and hammer a new pin and a fresh edge for the skinning blade. The hunter runs a thumb along it, grins, and presses stones and a few good hides on you.

encounters.name: The Haunted Furrow
encounters.text: At the forest's edge a farmer's barley field lies half trampled in a perfect spiral. A weak field-spirit, grown petty from neglect, is knocking over the stalks and giggling in the wind. The farmer begs you to make it stop before the harvest is lost.

choices.label: Chase the spirit off with a stick
choices.text: You flail about until the giggling fades. The spiral stays, but the worst of the barley is saved, and the farmer pays what he can.

choices.label: Leave the farmer to his luck
choices.text: You shrug and go on. Behind you the wind picks up and the stalks begin to fall again.

choices.label: Paste a ward on the scarecrow
choices.text: You ink a ward on blank paper, nail it to the scarecrow's chest and speak the closing phrase. The spirit squeals once and settles into the straw, bound to guard what it was ruining. The farmer is thrilled.

choices.label: Set a small array of stakes around the field
choices.text: You drive nine ash stakes at the field's corners and cut a thin ring of lines between them. The spirit circles once, finds no gap, and gives up with a sulky whistle. The farmer pays in stones and a basket of herbs.

encounters.name: The Snared Fox Kit
encounters.text: A hunter's wire snare has closed on a silver-furred fox kit beside the forest path. Its tail glows faintly, the mark of a young spirit beast, and it snaps weakly at anything that comes near. The hunter's footprints are fresh and not far off.

choices.label: Cut the wire and let it run
choices.text: You snip the snare and step back. The kit stares at you once, then bolts into the ferns.

choices.label: Leave it for the hunter
choices.text: It is not your snare and not your quarrel. You walk on, and the kit's thin cries follow you down the path.

choices.label: Sell the kit to a pelt dealer
choices.text: You carry the struggling kit to a dealer at the forest road, who counts out a handful of stones without meeting its eyes.

choices.label: Calm it, feed it, and ease the wire off
choices.text: You crouch low, hum the slow breath-song the old tamers use, and offer a pellet from your pouch. The kit trembles, eats, and lets you loosen the snare. It licks your wrist and slips away, but leaves a tuft of glowing fur behind, and the hunter, finding the empty snare, pays you to take his traps elsewhere.

encounters.name: The Charcoal Burners' Fever
encounters.text: A charcoal burner's family huddles around a smoking clamp deep in the mist. The youngest is burning with fever, and a mist fox has been circling their stores each night, bold with hunger. The father has no coin and asks nothing, only watches you with red-rimmed eyes.

choices.label: Calm them with a steady word and watch the night
choices.text: You sit up with the fever through the dark, keeping your spirit still so the fox keeps its distance. By dawn the child sleeps, and the family empties a small pouch into your hands.

choices.label: Brew a fever remedy from your satchel
choices.text: You boil spirit herb and dew grass in their clay pot until the broth runs clear. The fever breaks by morning, and the father presses a bundle of charcoal-roasted herbs on you.

choices.label: Wait for the fox and drive it off
choices.text: You hide among the charcoal stacks and wait. When the fox slinks in, you step out of the dark.

choices.label: Take what stores they have and move on
choices.text: You lift a sack of dried herbs from the lean-to while the father tends his child. The fox will have the rest.

encounters.text: Following a goat track above the herb slope, you push through a bramble hedge into a walled garden gone to seed. An old herbalist's tools still hang in the lean-to, and the beds he tended have kept growing without him.
A loose flagstone behind a noodle stall sounds hollow. Beneath it a ladder drops into a smugglers' tunnel under the lanes, long abandoned, its last crates still stacked against the wall.

Rope-climbing a cliff the sect disciples avoid, you find a cave mouth sealed by wind. Inside sits a skeleton in faded blue robes, a sword across its knees, and the stone walls are scored with cuts so clean they still hum.

encounters.name: The Ferryman's Token
encounters.text: A skeletal ferryman poles a rotten skiff out of the fog and stops beside you, one bony hand holding out a token of black jade. 'The Yin King's gate opens once in twelve years,' the dead voice says. 'The fare is not stones.'

choices.label: Pay the fare with a year of your life
choices.text: You let the ferryman take a year from you, cold as a drowned hand on your wrist. He bows to his new passenger and pushes the token into your hand.

choices.label: Pay the fare with 400 spirit stones
choices.text: The ferryman weighs the stones in his bony palm, finds them acceptable, and sinks them into the black water. The token is yours.

choices.label: Lay the ferryman's bones to rest
choices.text: You speak the words for the dead and burn the skiff. The ferryman crumbles, content, and the token he held is left on the water for you.

choices.label: Refuse and walk on
choices.text: The skiff slips back into the fog without a sound.

choices.label: Ease the ferryman's long grievance
choices.text: You read the drowned man's old wounds, the ones that never closed, and ease them with needle and quiet words. He weeps without tears, gives you the token and a pouch of the pills the dead once left in his skiff.

encounters.text: When the black water sinks in the dry month, a roofline rises from the mud: a drowned shrine to some forgotten river god, its altar still crowded with offerings the dead once left.

choices.label: Right the altar and pray for the dead
choices.text: You clear the silt, set the fallen idol upright and speak the old words over the bones. The yin qi in the water settles, and something grateful leaves a small gift behind.

choices.label: Strip the altar of its offerings
choices.text: The offerings are jade and bone and black pearl. You pocket the best of them, and the water behind you begins to boil softly.

choices.label: Relay the drowned shrine's ward array
choices.text: The shrine's boundary stones still hold the bones of an old river-warding array. You re-cut the broken lines, seat the black pearls as eyes and wake it. The water falls still, and the river god's thanks arrives as a gift of jade and calm.

encounters.text: Behind a shelf of fallen stone on the ridge, claw marks as tall as a house mark the mouth of a lair. The beast king that dug it is long gone, and it left behind the hoard it could not carry.
Deep in a gorge, a cliff face is scarred by a single ancient sword stroke. You sit before it for seven days, and the intent within the cut seeps into your mind.
A lightning-split tree, dead for centuries, has put out a single green shoot. Watching it, you glimpse something about life itself.
Two farming families have stopped speaking over a boundary stone, and the village elders ask the one name everyone trusts to walk the field with them and say where it belongs.

choices.label: Walk the boundary and judge fairly
choices.text: You pace the old furrows with both families watching and set the stone where the oldest ditch ran. Neither side is pleased, both accept, and the elders press a purse on you.

choices.label: Decline; it is no business of a cultivator
choices.text: The elders nod slowly and thank you for your time.

encounters.text: You spot a spirit stone glinting in a ditch.

encounters.name: The Granary Blessing
encounters.text: The headman waits at your door with his hat in both hands. The new granary is finished, the harvest is in, and rats and damp took half of last year's grain. He asks, very humbly, whether the immortal would lay a ward on the beams.

choices.label: Ward the granary
choices.text: You walk the beams once, pressing a thread of qi into each post. The villagers watch from the lane as though you were hanging the moon. The headman empties the village purse into your sleeve, and no one lets you refuse.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.text: You tell him a granary is kept by good tar and sharp cats, not by a cultivator's qi. He laughs, a little relieved, and bows you out.

encounters.name: Two Hopeful Youths
encounters.text: Two youths from {villager}'s field stand in your path, scuffed knees and shining eyes, and they have clearly argued over who would speak first. In the end they both bow at once and beg for pointers.

choices.label: Teach them a few forms
choices.text: You spend three days correcting their stance and their breath. Neither will ever feel qi, but they will walk straighter for it, and {villager} will not forget it.

choices.label: Send them to the sect hall
choices.text: You write a few words of introduction for the sect hall's gate and press a token into their hands. If the elders there are in a kind mood, they may be tested.

encounters.name: Something at the Fold
encounters.text: Three nights running, {villager} the shepherd has found hurdles broken and rams gored. Something with spiralled antlers and a pale hide comes down from the ridge when the moon is up. {villager} asks if you might keep watch; otherwise a hunter must be hired.

choices.label: Keep watch at the fold
choices.text: You sit among the sheep through the cold hours until the elk comes down the ridge, breath smoking, and lowers its antlers at you.

choices.label: Pay a hunter to see to it
choices.text: You press stones into the shepherd's hand for a hunter from the valley. The beast is gone in three nights, and {villager} blesses your name.

encounters.name: The Breath-Walker
encounters.text: A lean traveller in patched robes sits on a stump at the edge of the path, eating cold millet from a cloth. No sect badge hangs at his belt. He glances at the way you carry your breath and grins. "Nobody taught you that, did they? Me neither. Sit. I will show you what the road taught me."

choices.label: Sit and learn his way of breathing
choices.text: He has you breathe with your steps, in for four paces, out for six, until the rhythm stops being yours and becomes the hill's. By dusk your dantian is warmer than a day of sitting would make it. He waves off thanks and walks on, whistling, owing nothing to anyone.

choices.label: Share your food and talk of the road
choices.text: You trade your rice cakes for his stories: a ford that floods without warning, a hermit who pays in pills for firewood. He asks nothing in return, and you part as equals.

encounters.name: The Riverside Barter
encounters.text: Below the footbridge a handful of loose cultivators have spread oilcloth on the gravel and laid out their goods: bundled roots, chipped jade, a few sealed pill vials. No sect takes a tithe here and no elder checks the weights. An old woman with a missing finger beckons you over. "New to the road? We trade fair. Spirit Herbs for a pill, two for one, take it or leave it."

choices.label: Trade 2 Spirit Herbs for a Qi Gathering Pill
choices.text: She weighs the herbs in her palm, nods, and presses a vial into yours. "Come back when you have more. Nobody here will ask whose banner you stand under."

choices.label: Decline and just listen to the gossip
choices.text: You buy nothing, but you sit on a flat stone and hear which roads are safe this month and which sect patrols to avoid. The old woman does not mind; news is the cheapest thing on the gravel.

encounters.name: The Grey-Robed Recruiter
encounters.text: A woman in a neat grey robe falls into step beside you on the road, a sect token swinging at her hip. "I am not here to sell you anything," she says. She describes it plainly: halls with roofs that do not leak, a lecture every month, a pill for the breakthrough if you earn it, and in return a duty roster, a master's word that is law, and a seat you cannot leave without a reckoning. "Some people want that. Some do not. Both are honest roads." She bows and turns back before you have to answer.

encounters.name: The Cave-Swap Board
encounters.text: On a flat rock where three paths meet, loose cultivators have pinned strips of bark with scrawled notices: caves to let, ore wanted, a map for a map. No sect seal stamps the board and nobody keeps its ledger. A one-eyed man minding it taps a strip. "Three bars of plain iron ore, and I will tell you where the mist parts in the Misty Forest. Fair swap, or walk on."

choices.label: Trade 3 Iron Essence for his rumour
choices.text: He pockets the ore and draws a crooked line in the dust with his boot: past the old fir, left at the split stone, and keep walking when the path seems to end. "Don't thank me. Pin a notice of your own someday."

choices.label: Decline and read the notices
choices.text: You keep your ore and read the board instead: a cave that floods in spring, a hermit who wants salt, a warning about a patrol. The one-eyed man grunts approval; free people read before they trade.

encounters.name: The Wandering Master
encounters.text: An old cultivator sits on a boulder above the trail with a gourd across his knees, watching you climb. No banner, no badge, only a stillness that makes the wind seem to wait. "You stand like a man who taught himself," he calls down. "Half of it is good. Come, let me show you the other half."

choices.label: Let him correct your stance
choices.text: He walks around you twice, nudges a heel, presses a knuckle between your shoulder blades. When the qi settles into the new line it runs smoother than it has in months. He shoulders his gourd and is gone before you can offer anything in return.

choices.label: Politely keep your own way
choices.text: You thank him and say your stance is the road you built. He laughs, long and warm, and tells you that is the only answer he respects. He leaves you a swallow from his gourd and a line to think about on the way down.

encounters.name: The Shared Night Watch
encounters.text: Three loose cultivators have banked a fire in the lee of a rock, and one of them lies wrapped in a cloak, grey with pain from a fall. "We trade the watch by turns," says the eldest. "Nobody here owes a sect a debt, and nobody sleeps unguarded. Will you take a turn, or help us with him?"

choices.label: Tend the wounded one
choices.text: You spend the night binding his leg and feeding him broth from your own pack. By dawn his colour is back, and the three of them swear, in the plain way of the road, that you will find a fire and a meal wherever they camp.

choices.label: Take a turn on the watch
choices.text: You sit up with the fire until the stars turn, listening for the wrong kind of silence. Nothing comes. The eldest passes you a share of their dried fruit and a pinch of spirit stones for the hours, no questions asked.

encounters.name: A Name for the Newborn
encounters.text: A young mother stands in your doorway with a swaddled bundle, her husband fidgeting behind her. The midwife says a child named by an immortal grows up lucky, and they have waited three days for you to wake from meditation.

choices.label: Give the child a name
choices.text: You think of the first light on the ridge and give them a name that means just that. The mother says it over and over, softly, as though afraid it might fly away. The village will speak of this for years.

choices.label: Decline kindly
choices.text: You tell them a name should come from the people who will call it across a field at dusk. The mother smiles, a little embarrassed, and carries the child home.

encounters.name: The Peak Rogue's Plea
encounters.text: A ragged rogue cultivator waits at the well with a cracked sword and the sallow look of someone who has stood at the Ninth Layer for ten years. He bows lower than his pride allows and asks, with no hope in his voice, how one crosses into Foundation Establishment.

choices.label: Share your insight
choices.text: You spend three days walking the lanes with him, describing how your own qi turned dense and still. He says nothing for a long time, then kneels in the dust. Whether he crosses or not, he leaves a different man, and {villager}, who lent him a bed, thanks you for it.

choices.label: Ask for payment
choices.text: You name a price. He pays it from a pouch sewn into his lining, every coin he owns, and you tell him what you can. He thanks you without meeting your eyes.

encounters.name: The Junior Come Home
encounters.text: A young disciple in your sect's grey-blue robes waits at the village gate, home for the festival and a little lost. Their qi runs ragged around the fifth layer, and they ask, scarlet to the ears, whether the senior might spare an hour to look at it.

choices.label: Walk through their circulation
choices.text: You sit with them under the old pear tree and trace the stalls in their breath until the knot loosens. They bow three times, and {villager} sends a basket of dumplings to your door that evening.

choices.label: Send them to the elders
choices.text: You tell them the elders at the sect are paid in pills to answer such questions. They go away stiffly, and you feel the weight of the look.

encounters.name: A Guard for the Night
encounters.text: A grain merchant's wagon train has halted at the village inn, and the hired guard has a fever. The merchant spots your robes and offers a night's pay to keep watch, since the road ahead has been thick with sneak-thieves.

choices.label: Keep watch till dawn
choices.text: You sit on a wagon shaft with your senses spread thin. Twice shadows slip along the hedge and turn back at the touch of your qi. The merchant pays as promised and adds a little more.

choices.label: Ask for the wagon's best cargo instead
choices.text: You haggle shamelessly, and the merchant, who has no other watchman, gives way. The night is quiet and the pay is rich, but his goodwill is gone.

choices.label: Decline; you have your own rest to keep
choices.text: He mutters and walks off to find a drunk with a cudgel instead.

encounters.name: A Quarrel Over the Water Channel
encounters.text: The headman brings you to the dike, where a family that sends its sons to your sect and a farmer with three sour fields stand glaring over a cut water channel. Each says the other stole the flow. The headman begs the immortal to rule, since neither will hear him.

choices.label: Rule fairly after walking both fields
choices.text: You walk the channel from source to sluice and find the truth sat in the middle: a silted bend took the water from both. You have it dug out together, and both sides leave grumbling at each other, not you. {villager} calls it the fairest ruling in a generation.

choices.label: Side with the sect family
choices.text: The farmer's face closes like a fist. The sect family sends a fat purse to your door and a younger son to run your errands for a month.

choices.label: Refuse to meddle
choices.text: You tell them a cultivator's word is no tool for ditches. The headman sighs and finds a surveyor in the next village.

encounters.name: The Monk at the Well
encounters.text: A wandering monk in a threadbare robe crouches at the village well with his palm held flat above the water. Without looking up, he says that the well hums, and asks if the cultivator would lay a hand beside his and tell him what they feel.

choices.label: Join him and listen
choices.text: Your palm tingles with a faint, old pulse, as of a stone laid down by someone long gone. The monk smiles and gives you the savour of what he has learned in forty years of listening to wells.

on_fail.text: You feel cold water and nothing more. The monk pats your shoulder kindly and goes on down the road.

choices.label: Leave him to it
choices.text: You nod and go on your way. The hum, you suppose, is the village's business.

encounters.name: The Well Hums
encounters.text: At dusk the old well hums like a struck bell, and the children say the water has gone warm. A thread of spirit vein deep under Qingshi has stirred in its sleep, and its qi rises through the stones as though it were glad of company.
A wild boar charges out of the fields!
The hunters' guild has lost three dogs to a den under a fallen cedar, and its master sends word that only someone of your standing could be asked to clear it.

choices.label: Take the job and clear the den
choices.text: You find the den by its smell and go in.

choices.label: Not today
choices.text: The guild will find someone else, or wait.

encounters.text: The master of a caravan guild finds you among the stalls. A shipment of spirit ore must reach the Misty Forest road by dusk, and he would trust no one else with it.

choices.label: Escort the shipment
choices.text: You walk beside the lead cart until the forest road, and the guild master pays in full and speaks your name to the other caravans.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.text: The guild master bows and finds a lesser guard.

encounters.text: Two minor sects have quarrelled over a ledge of cloud-sea orchids and agreed on a duel. Neither trusts the other's elder to judge it, but both trust the name you carry.

choices.label: Judge the duel fairly
choices.text: You watch every exchange and call the winner by the rules both sides swore to. The loser grumbles and the winner's elder presses a purse of stones into your hand.

choices.label: Quietly favour the sect that pays you
choices.text: A hint of stones, a hand raised a heartbeat late, and the verdict falls where you wished. Few notice, but the loser's disciples do.

choices.label: Refuse to judge
choices.text: The elders sigh and settle it with swords.

encounters.text: Fisherfolk from the marsh edge kneel in the mud. A corpse refiner has been taking their dead from the graves at night, and they beg the cultivator they have heard so much about to end him.

choices.label: Hunt the corpse refiner
choices.text: You follow the grave-dirt trail to a bone-pole hut and break his puppets before he can finish his work. The villagers pour out what they have.

choices.label: Offer to buy his craft instead
choices.text: The refiner is glad to sell a few scraps of grave-iron wire and a lesson. The villagers will never know.

choices.label: Tell them it is not your concern
choices.text: They bow their heads and go back to their nets.

encounters.text: A grey-muzzled spirit ape steps onto the ledge and, in halting human speech, asks the cultivator who is known even here to carry a truce between the beast clans and the miners' guild.

choices.label: Carry the truce to the miners
choices.text: The guild grumbles but agrees, and a clan elder leaves a cache of crystals where you stand.

choices.label: Ask a price for your trouble
choices.text: The ape's lip curls, but it pays, and you carry the truce with less warmth than it deserved.

choices.label: Refuse and walk on
choices.text: The ape watches you go without a word.

choices.label: Speak for both clans as a tamer
choices.text: You know how a beast clan counts a debt, and you put it to the guild in terms the elders respect. The truce is sworn on both sides, and the ape's clan pays in stones and trust.

encounters.text: A bandit steps onto the road, blade drawn.
A ragged old man shares a breathing method before vanishing. Was he an immortal?
You gather spirit herbs from the misty undergrowth.
Deep in the valley you unearth a centuries-old blood ginseng!
The mist thickens and you lose your way for a week.
Glowing eyes in the mist: a pack of mist wolves!
A rogue cultivator eyes your storage pouch and attacks.
You find a small spirit vein and absorb it before it disperses.
A wandering doctor tends your wounds and refuses payment.
Fingers brush your sleeve. You catch the wrist before it slips away: a skinny youth with quick hands and terrified eyes, your pouch already half out of your sleeve.

choices.label: Hand him over to the guards
choices.text: You march him to the guardhouse. The stallholders he has robbed for months cheer you all the way.

choices.label: Make him empty his pockets
choices.text: He turns out his pockets: stones lifted from half the market. You keep every one and send him off with a kick.

choices.label: Let him go with a warning
choices.text: He bows until his forehead touches the stones. 'I won't forget this, immortal!' Then he is gone into the crowd. {villager}, who saw it all from a stall, nods to you.

encounters.text: The pickpocket you let go slides onto the bench beside you in a teahouse. 'You were kind to me, so here is something only the guild knows: the red door behind the dyers' street. Three knocks, a pause, two more.' He grins and is gone before your tea cools.
In an alley behind the dyers' street stands a red door with no handle. Voices murmur behind it, and the smell of pill smoke.

choices.label: Knock the thieves' signal
choices.text: Three knocks, a pause, two more. A slot opens, a pair of eyes looks you over, and the door swings in on a cramped thieves' market. You buy a Foundation Establishment Pill at a thief's price, no questions asked.

choices.label: Kick the door in
choices.text: The door gives on the second kick. The men inside are not pleased to see you.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: Some doors are better left closed. You walk on.

encounters.text: A woman in crimson falls into step beside you, smelling faintly of iron. 'The blood on your hands sings. The Blood Lotus Sect does not ask where power comes from, only that you take it.'

choices.label: Accept the blood-red lotus token
choices.text: She presses a warm lotus token into your palm. 'Show it at our gates and they will open. Do not show it to the Azure Cloud dogs.'

choices.label: Ask for a taste of the blood path
choices.text: She laughs and drops a dark red pill into your hand. 'A gift. The next one you will have to earn.'

choices.label: Send her away
choices.text: She shrugs and melts into the crowd. 'We will meet again. Your kind always comes to us in the end.'

encounters.text: An old man with snow-white brows has watched you for a while. When you finally notice him, he smiles: an Azure Cloud elder, wandering in plain clothes. 'A clear heart is rarer than a heavenly root these days. Ask, and I will give what I can.'

choices.label: Ask him to point out your flaws
choices.text: He watches you circulate your qi and taps three points on your back. Knots you never knew you had come undone.

choices.label: Ask for a letter of recommendation
choices.text: He writes a few lines in a flowing hand and seals them with his thumbprint. 'Give this to any Azure Cloud elder.'

choices.label: Ask for nothing
choices.text: He laughs until his beard shakes and leaves a pill on the table anyway. 'That answer is worth more than anything I could give.'

encounters.text: Driven mad by the beast tide, a pack of mist wolves pours out of the fog straight at you.
The ground shakes: an iron-horned rhino crashes through the trees at the head of the beast tide.
In the wake of the tide, trampled herb beds and dead beasts litter the ground. You gather what is still good.
A band of mortal hunters is pinned against a cliff by the beast tide, spears shaking.

choices.label: Hold the line with them
choices.text: You fight beside them until the beasts break off. They will tell this story for years.

choices.label: Use them as bait and slip past
choices.text: While the beasts tear into the hunters, you walk on unhurt.

choices.label: Leave them to it
choices.text: You are not their keeper.

encounters.text: Drums thunder around the tournament ring. The referee calls for challengers.

choices.label: Enter the ring
choices.text: You vault into the ring. Your opponent grins and draws his sword.

choices.label: Watch the bouts
choices.text: You watch the bouts from the stands, and the clash of so many arts opens your eyes.

choices.label: Move on
choices.text: You leave the crowd to its cheering.

encounters.text: The senior bracket begins. The reigning champion waits in the ring, arms folded.

choices.label: Challenge the champion
choices.text: The stands fall silent as you step up to the champion.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: Today is not your day for glory.

encounters.text: A harried appraiser, drowning in consignments, offers you a sealed jade box from the overflow for 150 spirit stones, contents unknown.

choices.label: Buy the jade box (150 spirit stones)
choices.text: You pry the box open: a lump of star silver, worth a little more than you paid.

choices.label: Pass
choices.text: You leave the box for someone luckier.

encounters.text: The streets are packed shoulder to shoulder with collectors. Somewhere in the crush, a light-fingered hand finds your pouch.
A blood-robed scout of the incursion spots you and licks his lips.
Blood Lotus raiders sweep down the road, harvesting everyone in their path. One of them turns toward you.
A column of refugees flees the demonic raiders: old men, mothers, children clutching what they could carry.

choices.label: Escort them to safety
choices.text: You walk them to the next town and keep watch through the night. A grandmother presses a coin into your hand and will not take it back, and her grandson swears he will repay you.

choices.label: Rob the refugees
choices.text: You take what little they have. They are too frightened to resist.

choices.label: Let them pass
choices.text: They shuffle past you without a word.

encounters.text: Blood on the grass leads you to a young cultivator slumped against a pine, robbed and half-dead. The bandits who did it are still going through his pack.

choices.label: Drive off the bandits
choices.text: You step out of the trees. The bandits' leader decides to try his luck.

choices.label: Wait until they leave, then bind his wounds
choices.text: When the bandits have gone, you clean and bind his wounds and sit with him through the fever.

choices.label: Leave him to his fate
choices.text: It is not your fight. You slip away before anyone sees you.

choices.label: Let them finish, then strip the body
choices.text: You wait in the trees. When the bandits leave, there is little left, but little is something.

encounters.text: A scream from the river: a child has slipped into the fast water below the mill, and the current is pulling her toward the weir.

choices.label: Dive in after her
choices.text: The water is cold enough to stop your heart, but you reach her before the weir. Her father, a woodcutter, falls to his knees on the bank, and {villager}, who ran down from the mill, wraps her in a blanket.

choices.label: Shout for the miller and walk on
choices.text: {villager} runs out with a rope. You do not stay to see how it ends.

encounters.text: In an alley behind the gambling dens, three thugs have cornered a young merchant over a debt that has doubled twice since breakfast.

choices.label: Pay the debt (30 spirit stones)
choices.text: You count out the stones. The thugs shrug and leave; the merchant stares at you as if you had fallen from heaven.

choices.label: Beat the thugs
choices.text: Their leader cracks his knuckles and comes at you.

choices.label: Help the thugs collect
choices.text: You hold the merchant still while they empty his purse. They toss you a share.

choices.label: Not your business
choices.text: You walk on. Behind you, something breaks.

encounters.text: {rival} strolls past with a crowd of admirers and stops to look you over. 'Still crawling through the lower layers? We started on the same day, you know. How embarrassing for you.'

choices.label: Swallow the insult
choices.text: You bow your head and let {rival} laugh. One day the heavens will turn.

choices.label: Answer with your fists
choices.text: You step forward. {rival}'s smile widens.

choices.label: Flatter {rival} shamelessly
choices.text: You heap praise on {rival} until even the admirers wince. It works: {rival} tosses you a coin and walks on.

encounters.text: {rival} blocks your path, eyes bright. 'Same realm again, are we? Then let us settle which of us the heavens favor.'

choices.label: Accept the duel
choices.text: You face each other in a ring of onlookers.

choices.label: Propose a contest of meditation instead
choices.text: You sit back to back until dawn, circulating qi. Neither yields; both of you rise a little stronger, and {rival} almost smiles.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: 'Coward,' {rival} says, and spits at your feet.

encounters.text: {rival} waves you over, grinning. 'Same realm again! Come, trade a few forms with me. No grudge, only the Way.'

choices.label: Trade a few forms
choices.text: You bow, and the two of you circle in the open air, blows pulled short of the bone.

choices.label: Share tea and talk of cultivation instead
choices.text: You sit on a warm rock and compare notes until the light fades. Both of you rise a little stronger.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.text: 'Another day, then,' {rival} says, unbothered.

encounters.text: Envy has eaten at {rival} since you pulled ahead. Tonight it shows: {rival} leaps from the shadows, blade drawn.
In the teahouse everyone is talking about {rival}, who has reached {rival_realm}. The name stings.

At the herb seller's stall you are counting out coins for the last Qi Gathering Pill when {rival} reaches over your shoulder and drops a silver tael on the counter. 'I'll take that,' {rival} says, as if you were a post.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.text: You step aside. {rival} pockets the pill without a glance, and the herb seller gives you an apologetic shrug.

choices.label: Outbid {rival} (12 spirit stones)
choices.text: You slap twelve spirit stones on the counter. The herb seller's eyes widen; {rival}'s jaw tightens, and the pill is yours.

choices.label: Demand the pill
choices.text: 'It was mine first.' {rival} turns slowly, and the crowd clears a space around the two of you.

encounters.text: A wolf hunt has gone badly wrong. You find {rival} slumped against a mossy trunk, robes torn, a satchel of freshly cut herbs spilled in the ferns. The wolves are long gone; {rival} has not seen you yet.

choices.label: Bind {rival}'s wounds
choices.text: You wash and bind the wounds and share your water. {rival} says nothing, but the look is not hatred.

choices.label: Take the herbs
choices.text: You scoop up the herbs and leave {rival} to the mist. A weak hand clutches at your sleeve; you shake it off.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: It is not your quarrel. You leave the clearing as quietly as you entered it.

encounters.text: It is the sect's monthly lecture. The elder lets a long silence hang, then asks a question about the circulation of true qi. {rival} answers first, crisply, and glances back at you with a small smile.

choices.label: Answer better than {rival}
choices.text: You rise and take {rival}'s answer apart, then build a truer one in its place, tying the circulation to the breath of the mountain itself. The elder sets down his cup. The hall is silent; {rival} lowers their eyes, and the insight settles deep in your dantian.

choices.label: Give a better answer
choices.text: You rise and correct one detail, then add another the elder had not mentioned. The elder strokes his beard; the lecture hall hums, and the insight settles deep in your dantian.

choices.label: Stay quiet
choices.text: You keep your eyes on your cushion and listen. The elder's words are worth more than your pride.

encounters.text: At the Herb & Ore Stall a single Cloud-Mist Orchid sits on a bed of damp moss, its petals half mist. You reach for it, and a hand beats yours there. {rival} smiles without warmth. 'Name your price, stallkeeper. Mine is higher than whatever this one offers.'

choices.label: Let it go
choices.text: You withdraw your hand. Foundation Establishment is long enough to wait for another orchid; {rival} will not always be ahead.

choices.label: Outbid {rival} (60 spirit stones)
choices.text: You count out sixty stones into the stallkeeper's palm. {rival}'s smile thins to a line, but the orchid is yours.

choices.label: Walk away with a cold word
choices.text: 'Enjoy it,' you say, and let the silence do the rest. {rival} stares after you all the way to the end of the lane.

encounters.text: A howl rolls across the reeds, then a cry that you know too well: {rival} is calling your name. Backed against a dead tree, sword shaking, {rival} faces a blood-eyed wolf with nowhere left to run.

choices.label: Save {rival}
choices.text: You step between them and draw. The wolf's red eyes swing to you.

choices.label: Leave {rival} to the marsh
choices.text: You turn away. Behind you, the cry rises once, and then it is only the wind in the reeds.

encounters.text: {rival} is waiting on the sect's practice terrace, sleeves bound, a crowd of disciples already gathering. 'Same realm, same sect hall. Let them see which of us is the real Foundation talent.'

choices.label: Accept the challenge
choices.text: You bow, and step onto the flagstones. The disciples fall silent.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: 'Another day,' you say. {rival} shrugs, and the crowd drifts apart.

encounters.text: {rival} finds you at dusk, alone and without a blade. 'You were always one step ahead. I hated you for it. Maybe it is time I stopped.'

choices.label: Share a jar of wine and let the past go
choices.text: You drink until the stars come out. By morning, the old rivalry feels like a story about two other people.

choices.label: Turn your back
choices.text: You walk away. {rival}'s shoulders sag.

encounters.text: {rival} is sitting on a flat rock by the road, a clay pot of millet porridge steaming between two bowls. 'I made too much,' {rival} says, a little too casually. 'Sit. And I have been turning over a thought about the circulation of qi that I would like to hear you pick apart.'

choices.label: Accept a Qi Gathering Pill instead
choices.text: 'Take it,' {rival} says, pressing a small wax-sealed pill into your palm. 'I would rather you owe me nothing, and still take it.'

choices.label: Share the meal and trade insights
choices.text: You eat, and talk until the fire burns low. {rival}'s idea is rough but sound, and yours smooths it; you both walk away with something the other lacked.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.text: You bow and walk on. {rival} watches you go, then eats both bowls alone.

encounters.text: The patch of spirit herbs you have tended for weeks has been trampled flat and sprinkled with salt. Fresh footprints lead away, and in the village the whisper is already going round that you steal herbs from others. {rival} is leaning on a fence nearby, watching your face.

choices.label: Settle it with fists
choices.text: You cross the distance in three strides. {rival} was waiting for exactly this.

choices.label: Pay 30 spirit stones to settle it
choices.text: You press thirty stones into the village elder's hand to quiet the rumor and replant the patch. {rival} sneers, but the matter is closed.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.text: You replant what you can and keep your head down. Rumors rot faster than herbs.

encounters.text: {rival} climbs onto an overturned crate in the middle of the crowd and points straight at you. 'Everyone here knows the name of the one who thinks to stand above me. Come, show them what you are made of, or admit you are nothing.'

choices.label: Accept the challenge
choices.text: You step into the cleared circle and bow. The crowd's murmur dies.

choices.label: Decline before the crowd
choices.text: 'I have nothing to prove to you,' you say. Some of the crowd nod; more laugh. {rival} crows, and your name gets a little smaller.

encounters.text: A silver fox darts out of the fog and snaps at your heels, then circles for another go.
Mist parts around a stag whose bronze-ringing antlers lower toward you; you have wandered into the glade it has claimed.
The fog thickens and goes cold. A coil as thick as your waist slides across the path, and a wedge-shaped head rises out of the mist to taste the air near your face.
An iron-backed boar bursts out of a turnip field, bristles clanging like a rack of spears.
A reeking outer disciple lurches out of the wine shop, knocks over a fruit stall and demands the stallkeeper's purse. Then he sees you and draws his borrowed sword.
A blue shape drops out of the clouds: an azure crane, beak first.
Red eyes rise out of the reeds, then a second pair, then a wolf as big as a calf.
In a teahouse you overhear rumours of an ancient cave on Azure Peak.
Your pouch feels lighter. A pickpocket!
You win a game of stone-gambling and crack open a raw spirit stone.
A stone-skinned ape hurls a boulder at you!
The undergrowth splits and a boar with a hide like river stone lowers its tusks at you.
A shape drags itself out of the black water, green poison beading on its stiff fingers.
A drifting cultivator blocks the road out of the village. 'Your pouch, friend, or your pride.'
A cloud eagle dives from the heavens!
Watching the sea of clouds, you glimpse a fragment of the Dao.
In a sealed jade box beside a meditating skeleton rests a single fragrant pill. Its owner died waiting for a breakthrough; you will not.
Among the bones of a long-dead cultivator lies a jade slip.
A stone guardian awakens, its eyes burning with formation light.
You share your meal with a starving child. {villager}, who has been minding the child, presses a few stones into your hand, and Heaven seems to nod.
A hooded peddler sidles up and whispers of 'blood pills' that need no herbs, only lives. He opens his sleeve: a dark red pill that smells of iron.

choices.label: Buy a Blood Demon Pill
choices.text: You pay. The peddler grins and melts into the crowd. Somewhere, someone paid more.

choices.label: Seize him for the town guard
choices.text: You twist his arm behind his back and drag him to the guardhouse. The crowd cheers.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.text: You walk away, but the idea gnaws at you.

encounters.text: A rogue cultivator lies against a mossy trunk, his robe black with old blood. 'A pill,' he rasps. 'Anything that mends bone. I have nothing to give but my thanks.'

choices.label: Give him a Bone-Setting Salve
choices.text: You spread the salve over his shattered ribs. His breathing eases, and he grips your wrist with a rough hand. 'The Dao keeps no debts, but I will.'

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: You step past him. Behind you the rasping goes on a while, then stops.

encounters.text: A mortal woman hurries after you through the lanes, sobbing. Her small child burns with fever, and the village healer is three days away. 'You are a cultivator. Please.'

choices.label: Steep a Spirit Herb for the child
choices.text: You boil the herb down to a pale broth and hold the cup to the child's lips. By dusk the fever breaks. The mother kneels in the dust until you lift her up.

choices.label: Say you cannot help
choices.text: You mutter that mortal sickness is not your concern. The woman's face closes like a door.

encounters.text: A wandering alchemist crouches at the marsh edge, cursing at a cracked gourd of reagents. 'No spirit herb in a day's walk,' she mutters. 'Find me one and I will trade you something better: a hint most pill-masters pay years for.'

choices.label: Trade two Spirit Herbs for her hint
choices.text: She grinds the herbs into a bubbling paste and murmurs the secret of fire and timing as she works. You watch her hands, and something clicks into place.

choices.label: Keep your herbs
choices.text: She snorts and turns back to her gourd. 'Then keep your ignorance too.'

encounters.text: The villagers hold a harvest festival and press rice wine and dew grass on you as an honoured guest.
You catch a thief fleeing {villager}'s house and return what he stole. {villager} insists you take a reward.
A young cultivator lies against a tree, his side torn open by wolf claws. His storage pouch hangs from his belt, and he is far too weak to stop anyone.

choices.label: Bind his wounds and see him to safety
choices.text: You stop the bleeding and carry him to a woodcutter's hut. He presses two pills into your palm and swears he will not forget your face.

choices.label: Strip his pouch and leave him to the wolves
choices.text: You take everything he has. He curses you by name and by face as you walk away. The mist hides your crime, but not from him.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.text: It is not your karma. You walk on, and do not look back.

choices.label: Treat his wounds as a doctor would
choices.text: You clean the claw wounds, set the torn muscle and stitch it with spirit-silk. He wakes clear-eyed, tucks pills and stones into your hands and asks your name twice so he will not forget it.

encounters.text: A cultivator in sect robes hails you on the road: the traveller you once carried out of the forest. He has joined a sect, and he has not forgotten his debt.
A cultivator blocks the road, eyes red. 'My brother crawled home with nothing but your face in his memory. Today you pay.'

An Azure Cloud elder stops you at the gate. 'So you are the one who carried my disciple out of the forest. He speaks of you at every meal. The Azure Cloud Sect remembers its friends.' He presses a jade token of goodwill into your hand.

The sky darkens as a grey-robed elder descends on a flying sword. 'One of my disciples you robbed and left for the wolves. His brother you cut down when he came for justice. I have come for both debts.'
A dying cultivator presses a pill into your palm: 'Bury me, and live well.' You give him a quiet grave.
You find a wounded traveller too weak to resist. You strip his pouch and leave him to the wolves. The mist hides your crime.
A white fox sits beside a purple cloud mushroom and watches you. You leave it a share and it bows its head before vanishing.
A pocket of miasma rolls through the valley. You flee, coughing, and lose days recovering.
A blood-path cultivator steps from the trees, licking his lips at your qi.
A jade-scaled python lies coiled around a spirit herb. It lifts its head as you approach.
A righteous sect patrol shares fire and rations with you. Their elder tosses you a pill for the road.
An abandoned altar still hums with slaughter-qi. You drink it in; the power is real, and so is the stain on your soul.
A clear night, a falling star. You sit through the dawn and your breathing falls into a deeper rhythm.
Hired thugs corner you in an alley, sent by a merchant whose goods you outbid.
Sparks drift through the grass: a flame-tailed fox bares its teeth over a patch of flame lotus.
The ground shakes as an iron-horned rhino lowers its head and charges.
The mist turns bitterly cold. Frost-silk threads tighten around you as an ice-soul spider descends.
A ragged swordsman blocks the road. 'Draw your weapon. Let my sword see what you are.'
An Azure Cloud enforcer seizes your wrist. 'I sense demonic qi on you. Come quietly or be subdued!'
A red-robed Blood Lotus disciple circles you, smiling. 'The blood pools are thirsty, and you look full of essence.'
A coffin lid slides open. A bronze-skinned corpse rises, its joints grinding like millstones.
Storm clouds gather out of a clear sky. A thunderwing roc screams and dives at you, lightning in its wake.
The herb valley falls silent. A toad the size of a house blinks at you over a thousand-year lingzhi.
A roar shakes stones loose from the ridge. The Black Iron Bear King has noticed you on its mountain.
A red mist rolls over the road and condenses into a Blood Lotus elder. 'Core Formation essence. What a rare treat.'
Wailing fills the cave. Pale shades part, and a crowned ghost king rises from a throne of bones.
A wealthy auction house leaves cast-off ore in the sweepings. You buy it for nearly nothing.
A wanted poster offers a bounty on a demonic cultivator hiding in the mountain wilds. Perhaps someone brave will answer it.
A white-haired hermit shares tea and a single pointer on the Dao, then waves you away.
On a frozen cliff face, an ice soul flower blooms. The climb is brutal but worth it.
A rockslide buries the trail and you spend days digging free.
Beneath a toppled altar lies a scripture written in dried blood. Its first line promises power at the price of life. You take it.
A demonic cultivator's remains still clutch a pouch of spirit stones. Taking them feels like a quiet pact.
Behind a collapsed wall lies a sealed alchemy chamber. A jade case rests on the cold furnace, and the dead alchemist's lingering will still hovers over it, guarding the Core Forming Pill formula.

choices.label: Chant a rite to release his spirit
choices.text: The lingering will of a dead alchemist begs for release. You chant until it fades, and it leaves its life's formula, the Core Forming Pill, as thanks.

choices.label: Bow to the dead and open the jade case
choices.text: Behind a collapsed wall you find a sealed alchemy chamber. Its owner crumbled to dust long ago, but a jade case on the furnace still holds a formula for the Core Forming Pill.

choices.label: Shatter the spirit and devour it
choices.text: A dead alchemist's spirit clings to his furnace, guarding a scroll. You shatter it, devour what remains, and take the Core Forming Pill formula for yourself.

choices.label: Leave the dead in peace
choices.text: You bow once and leave the chamber sealed.

encounters.text: Restless ghosts wail among the ruins. You chant until they find peace, leaving behind a small gift.
A pit of stacked bones whispers to you. Wrapped around a skull is a skin-bound manual: a demonic sealing pit, and its prize.

choices.label: Pry the manual loose
choices.text: A pit of stacked bones whispers to you. Wrapped around a skull is a skin-bound manual. You pry it loose; the whispering turns to laughter.

choices.label: Burn the manual and lay the dead to rest
choices.text: You recognise a demonic sealing pit. You burn the cursed manual and chant a rite for the dead; the whispers fade and a faint blessing settles on you.

choices.label: Back away
choices.text: You back away from the pit. The whispers follow you a long way.

encounters.text: On a cracked altar rests a scripture that drinks the light. You know what it is: the Heaven Devouring Art, and what it costs.

choices.label: Take the scripture
choices.text: On a cracked altar rests a scripture that drinks the light. You know what it costs, and take it anyway.

choices.label: Shatter the altar and seal its hunger
choices.text: You shatter the altar and seal the scripture's hunger away with your own qi. Sages would approve.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.text: Some fortunes are better left untouched. You walk away.

encounters.text: An old woodcutter watches you spar with the trees, laughs, and presses a bundle of leaf-pages into your hands. 'The forest taught me. Let it teach you.'
Halfway up a cliff you find stance diagrams carved into the living rock by some long-dead body cultivator. You pry loose the clearest slab.
You spend days helping wandering monks rehang the great bell of a ruined temple. Before they move on, the abbot gives you their Golden Bell sutra.
A demonic cultivator lies dead in the brush, a blood-soaked manual clutched to his chest. The palm prints on its cover are still warm.

choices.label: Take the blood manual
choices.text: A demonic cultivator lies dead in the brush, a blood-soaked manual clutched to his chest. You pry it loose. The palm prints on its cover are still warm.

choices.label: Burn the manual with its owner
choices.text: You find a dead demonic cultivator and the blood manual he died for. You burn it with him so no one else follows his path.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: You leave the corpse to the crows.

encounters.text: In a sealed sword chamber, nine frozen swords circle a jade slip. When you touch it, the swords shatter into snow.
Where an earth dragon vein breaks the surface, a stele records how an ancient master tempered his body in its flow. You take rubbings of every line.
A mummified demonic elder sits cross-legged in a burial niche, festering with corpse qi, a silk-wrapped manual in his lap.

choices.label: Take the manual
choices.text: A mummified demonic elder sits cross-legged in a burial niche, a silk-wrapped manual in his lap. You take it while the corpse's grin seems to widen.

choices.label: Burn the corpse before it rises
choices.text: You find a demonic elder's corpse festering with corpse qi and burn it, manual and all, before it can rise. Your own qi is cleansed in the flames.

choices.label: Leave the niche
choices.text: You leave the elder to his long sleep.

encounters.text: Deep in the cave lies the tomb of an Azure Heaven sword sect patriarch. His sword intent tests you for five days, then yields its canon.
A black bone slip floats above a pit of shrieking souls. Whatever art is written on it, it is what binds them here.

choices.label: Reach through the screams and take it
choices.text: A black bone slip floats above a pit of shrieking souls. You reach through their screams and close your hand around it.

choices.label: Crush the slip and free the souls
choices.text: You crush the bone slip that binds a pit of tormented souls. They rise in a stream of light, and some of their gratitude flows into you.

choices.label: Leave the pit
choices.text: You leave the souls to their screaming.

encounters.text: Empty chambers and dust. Whatever was here is long gone.
A fallen talisman master's pouch lies in the grass, its owner long gone. A few talismans inside are still potent.
A Daoist altar still hums with stored lightning. Beside it, sealed in oiled cloth, lie unused talismans and fresh gold-thread paper.
A sword cultivator sits dead in meditation, a sheaf of talisman paper across his knees. His last sword intent is folded into the pages, with notes on how it was done.
A landslide has bared a seam of black profound iron. You spend days prying it loose with your bare qi.
A weathered grave marker on a lonely ridge reads 'Spear Saint Han'. The earth beneath it hums with old spear intent.

choices.label: Sweep the grave and kneel
choices.text: A weathered grave marker reads 'Spear Saint Han'. You sweep the grave and kneel. A spear rises from the earth and settles in your hands, as if it had been waiting for a worthy heir.

choices.label: Dig up the grave
choices.text: A lonely grave marker reads 'Spear Saint Han'. The dead need nothing. You dig him up and take his spear and burial stones.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: You nod to the dead saint and walk on.

encounters.text: Deep in the ruins an ancient forge still burns with dragon fire. On its anvil lies a jade slip of forging memories and two ingots of red-veined gold.
In a clearing where nothing grows, a crimson saber stands buried to the hilt in a mound of withered corpses. It hums as you draw near: Blood-Drinker.

choices.label: Pull the saber free
choices.text: In a clearing where nothing grows, a crimson saber stands buried to the hilt in a mound of withered corpses. It hums as you draw near. You pull it free and feel it taste you.

choices.label: Shatter the blade and free its souls
choices.text: A crimson saber stands in a mound of withered corpses, and you know its name: Blood-Drinker. You pour your qi into the blade until it cracks, and the souls trapped inside drift free.

choices.label: Leave the clearing
choices.text: You leave before the saber's hunger can turn on you.

encounters.text: In a coffin sealed with nine iron nails lies a corpse wrapped in grey spider silk that is colder than the stone around it.

choices.label: Strip the shroud and wear it
choices.text: In a coffin sealed with nine iron nails lies a corpse wrapped in grey silk that is colder than the stone around it. You strip the shroud from the dead and put it on.

choices.label: Burn the cursed shroud and bury the dead
choices.text: A coffin sealed with nine iron nails holds a corpse wrapped in cursed spider silk. You burn the shroud with true fire and bury the dead properly. The tomb's stale qi clears.

choices.label: Close the coffin
choices.text: You hammer the nails back in and leave.

choices.label: Unpick the curse and reforge the shroud
choices.text: You draw the nine nails and temper them in true fire, then rework the grey silk with their iron until the curse has nowhere to cling. The corpse is buried properly; the nine nails, reforged, are worth more than the shroud ever was.

encounters.text: At the heart of a sacrificial array a black banner flies in a wind that is not there. Ten thousand captive voices beg you to free them.

choices.label: Take the banner
choices.text: At the heart of a sacrificial array a black banner flies in a wind that is not there. Ten thousand voices beg you to free them. Instead you pick it up, and they begin to scream.

choices.label: Break the array and free the souls
choices.text: At the heart of a sacrificial array a black banner holds ten thousand captive souls. You break the array flag by flag over seven days. As the last soul passes on, its gratitude settles on your Dao heart.

choices.label: Leave the array
choices.text: You leave. The voices beg after you until the tunnel bends.

encounters.text: Wind tears the clouds open for a moment, and on a ledge no mortal could reach you see two snow lotuses white against the ice. You drift down on your qi and pluck them.
A faint pull on your spirit leads you to a crag where Nine-Leaf Soul Grass grows in the cracks of an old sword mark. You count the leaves twice before digging.
Beneath the cave floor the mountain's roots run with earth marrow. Pale fungus clings to them in clusters, and the air is thick enough to chew.
Above the cloud line you find a pool fed by snowmelt and starlight. A thousand-year lotus has dropped its seed pod; one golden seed still glows within.
An alchemist died here mid-refinement, slumped over her furnace. Under her hand lies a jade slip: the Soul Nourishing Pill formula.

choices.label: Take the jade slip
choices.text: An alchemist died here mid-refinement, her furnace still holding a soft grey glow. Under her hand is a jade slip: the Soul Nourishing Pill formula.

choices.label: Bury her with a senior's rites first
choices.text: A dead alchemist slumps over a cold furnace. You bury her with the rites owed to a senior, and when you return the jade slip in her grave-goods glows warmly, offering you her Soul Nourishing Pill formula.

choices.label: Leave her undisturbed
choices.text: You bow to the senior and leave her as she lies.

choices.label: Finish her last refinement and take the formula
choices.text: Her furnace still holds its grey glow. You read her half-written notes, finish the pill she could not, and bury her over the furnace with the rites owed to a senior. The jade slip warms in your hand, and her last batch is yours.

encounters.text: An alchemist died here mid-refinement, her furnace still holding a soft grey glow. Under her hand is a jade slip: the Soul Nourishing Pill formula.

A dead alchemist slumps over a cold furnace. You bury her with the rites owed to a senior, and when you return the jade slip in her grave-goods glows warmly, offering you her Soul Nourishing Pill formula.
The white-haired hermit sits by his teapot as if he never left. 'Still climbing? Good. I have an old breathing art no one has asked me for in three hundred years.'

choices.label: Kneel and ask to be taught
choices.text: You kneel on the cold stone for three days. On the fourth he laughs, and taps the art into your brow with one finger.

choices.label: Offer 300 spirit stones for it
choices.text: He weighs the pouch, snorts, and tosses you a jade slip. 'Fair. Mountains do not care how you pay.'

choices.label: Decline and move on
choices.text: You thank him for the tea and keep climbing.

encounters.text: A stone gate carved with nine thunderclouds blocks the way. Behind it, the last patriarch of a vanished storm sect left his inheritance, and a trial: sit under his lightning array and live.

choices.label: Sit beneath the lightning
choices.text: For ten days lightning pours through your meridians. On the tenth the gate opens and a jade slip drifts into your hands, crackling.

choices.label: Burn years of life to force the trial
choices.text: Your cultivation is too shallow, so you pay with your life force instead. You crawl out of the array grey-haired, the jade slip clutched to your chest.

choices.label: Come back when you are stronger
choices.text: The thunderclouds on the gate seem to rumble as you leave.

encounters.text: A hall of a thousand standing corpses, all facing a throne. On it sits a dried patriarch, a black jade canon in his lap. The air tastes of grave soil and stolen qi.

choices.label: Take the canon
choices.text: You pry the canon from the patriarch's fingers. A thousand heads turn to watch you leave.

choices.label: Burn the hall and the canon
choices.text: You fill the hall with true fire. The corpses fall one by one, and the stolen qi they held flows out, cleansed, into you.

choices.label: Leave the dead their throne
choices.text: You back out of the hall without turning around.

encounters.text: The white fox you once shared a mushroom with waits on a moonlit rock, three tails now swaying behind it. Lightning gathers above: it is facing its tribulation, and it is looking at you.

choices.label: Stand guard while it faces the lightning
choices.text: You turn aside the stray bolts with your own qi. When the clouds clear, the fox bows, and a single drop of silver blood falls into your palm before it rises into the sky.

choices.label: Strike while it is weakened
choices.text: You strike as the third bolt falls. The fox dies screaming, and you carve out its inner core and its silver blood. Heaven's lightning lingers over you a moment longer than it should.

choices.label: Leave it to its fate
choices.text: This is its trial, not yours. You walk away as thunder rolls behind you.

encounters.text: In a hidden valley lies a qilin, scales dulled, breath shallow, an arrow of black iron in its side. Its golden eyes follow you. Its blood smells of spring rain.

choices.label: Draw the arrow and tend it until the end
choices.text: You sit with the qilin for ten days. Before it dies it touches its horn to your brow, and something of its blood stays with you.

choices.label: Drink its heart's blood
choices.text: You open its chest while it still breathes. The blood burns going down, and the valley goes silent around you.

choices.label: Leave it in peace
choices.text: Some fortunes are not meant to be taken. You bow and leave the valley.

encounters.text: At the bottom of the ruins lies a pool of blood that never dried, where an Asura general was slain ten thousand years ago. It still boils, and it calls to you.

choices.label: Bathe in the Asura's blood
choices.text: You sink into the pool. For seven days you scream, and then you stop. You climb out with red-rimmed eyes and the Asura's madness in your veins.

choices.label: Seal the pool
choices.text: You burn talisman after talisman until the pool turns to black glass. The slaughter-qi it held disperses through your meridians, cleansed.

choices.label: Back away
choices.text: You leave the pool to boil in the dark.

encounters.text: Grey fog rolls over the black water. You wade for two days among drowned banners and find nothing but leeches.
A still pool, cold as a winter grave, seethes with yin qi. You sit at its edge and draw the chill into your meridians.
Pale corpse-lilies bloom on a sunken war chariot. Purple mushrooms crowd its rotten wheels.

A drowned cultivator's body has washed up against the reeds, a sect token still in his fist. You carry him to dry ground and bury him under a cairn. His lingering resentment eases, and so does your heart.
A drowned cultivator floats face-down in the reeds. You cut his storage pouch free and push the body back into the dark water.
A corpse-refiner's disciple rises from the reeds, three bloated puppets shambling behind him. 'Fresh material!'
Beneath a toppled war altar the water runs red with the blood essence of ten thousand dead. You open your meridians and drink it in. Your qi swells; something in your eyes does not come back.

Beneath a toppled war altar the water runs red with old blood essence. You chant the rites of passing for five days until the pool runs clear, and the freed souls leave a trace of their gratitude in your sea of qi.
A blood-robed cultivator steps across the water without making a ripple. 'The marsh's yin qi is mine. So is yours.'
The water bulges. A jade-scaled serpent, older than the battle that made this marsh, rises from the deep.
A drowned soldier lurches out of the mud, black thread still holding its jaw shut. Somewhere in the reeds, its master is watching.
The water goes still and bitterly cold. A pale shape rises from the black pool, mouth open in a wail you feel in your bones rather than hear.
A crimson-sashed figure crouches over a red pool, scratching in a notebook. He looks up, sees you, and reaches for his blade. 'Nobody was supposed to be out here.'
Under a shell of rust lies a commander's sword hilt still bound in cold iron and a pouch of ancient stones that kept their qi through the centuries.
A silent ferryman poles you across a channel and refuses payment. 'The dead pay me already,' he says, and is gone in the fog.
A storm breaks over a bare summit. Instead of fleeing, you sit among the strikes for five days and nights, and somewhere in the roar you hear the heavens' grammar.
A single leaf drifts through the mist and never seems to land. You follow it for three days, and when it finally settles, so does something in you.
A shattered teleportation array still flickers in the rubble. Where its lines break, the far side of the hall is somehow one step away. You study the fold until you can almost feel it.
Ten thousand broken weapons jut from the mud where two armies of cultivators annihilated each other. The killing intent still hangs in the air, thick enough to taste.

choices.label: Drink in the killing intent
choices.text: You open yourself to it. Ten thousand deaths pour into your sea of consciousness, and you come out the other side colder and stronger.

choices.label: Chant sutras to lay the dead to rest
choices.text: For seven days you chant until the last angry ghost falls silent. The calm left behind is as hard as diamond.

choices.label: Leave the dead to their quarrel
choices.text: Some things are better left unlearned. You skirt the field and go on your way.

choices.label: Salvage and reforge the best of the broken blades
choices.text: For four days you sort the mud-crusted weapons by the ring of the steel, and your hammer-eye finds a lump of profound iron in a general's shattered halberd. The rest sells for a fair price in scrap.

encounters.text: A wandering monk rings a cracked bronze bell at dawn. Each toll seems to strike your bones rather than your ears.

choices.label: Sit with the monk and listen
choices.text: Three days of bells and silence. When you rise, your body feels like a temple that no storm could shake.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: You nod to the monk and keep walking. The bell follows you for a while, then fades.

encounters.text: In a back street stands a smithy whose furnace has not gone out in three hundred years. The old smith lets you sit by it for five days; the flame never repeats itself.
Beneath a waterfall lies a boulder worn into a perfect bowl. You meditate under the torrent until you understand how the soft overcame the hard.
Locals swear the hill on the horizon was once a day's walk further west. You sit at its foot for seven days and feel it breathe, once.
An old woodcutter who has never cultivated a day in his life swings his axe without ever tiring. Watching how he breathes between strokes, you suddenly understand something simple and deep.
A crater of fused black glass, still stinking of ozone. At its heart kneels the charred body of a cultivator who failed the heavens, a talisman pouch clutched to their chest.

choices.label: Bury them and pray for their soul
choices.text: You raise a grave mound and burn incense. As the smoke rises, the pouch falls open on its own: a gift, freely given.

choices.label: Take the pouch and keep walking
choices.text: You pry the pouch from fingers of charcoal. A scorched jade slip and a talisman, a fair trade for a corpse that needs nothing.

choices.label: Strip the body and refine its remnant qi
choices.text: You crack the bones and draw out what lightning left of their Core. The pouch, the slip and a dead cultivator's last strength are yours.

choices.label: Distil the lightning-struck remnant into a pill
choices.text: You gather the scorched marrow and what the lightning left of the Core, and refine them over a dead cultivator's own cinders into a pill that carries their last peace. The pouch and its talisman are yours as well.

encounters.text: A Core Formation elder who just survived the heavens is in a generous mood and scatters the talismans they did not need to the crowd. One lands in your hands.
The cloud sea parts below you and a condor wider than a village rises out of it, mouth open to swallow the sky.
The rock under your feet is warm, then hot. Slag runs down the cliff, and a basilisk the colour of cooling iron uncoils from its vent.
What you took for a hill lifts its head. Ten thousand years of starlight look down at you out of an old shell, and it does not like trespassers.
A Nascent Soul elder descends on a sword of cold light. 'Demonic qi, stinking of slaughter. In the name of the Azure Law, kneel!'
An old man sits at a ruined crossroads with a rusted sword across his knees. 'Few come this way anymore. Draw, and let us see if you have an answer.'
The marsh water turns red from the horizon inwards. A Blood Sea deacon rides the tide, smiling. 'A Nascent Soul, ripe and alone. The sect thanks you.'
A cold bone-coloured flame swims toward you through the mist. 'Another soul to keep me company,' says the thing behind it, 'for another hundred years.'
Dust drifts from the vault door as you touch it. Behind it, a jade puppet opens eyes of star silver and raises a fist the size of a boulder.
In a cave above the cloud line sits a withered sect patriarch whose soul is guttering out. His eyes find you. 'Please. My inheritance, or my last breath. One of them must not be wasted.'

choices.label: Hear his last words and carry them to his sect
choices.text: He pours his life's regrets into your ear and dies smiling. You will deliver them, someday.

choices.label: Take his spirit stones and leave him to the dark
choices.text: You lift the storage ring from his unresisting finger. He says nothing at all.

choices.label: Drain the last of his soul
choices.text: His Nascent Soul comes apart in your hands like wet paper. The qi is vast, and bitter.

encounters.text: A talisman-wrapped jade bottle sits on an altar, humming. A voice from within offers you bargains in a hundred honeyed tongues.

choices.label: Reseal it with a stronger seal
choices.text: You burn your own qi into the seals until the voice goes quiet. The bottle will outlast you.

choices.label: Smash the bottle and take what it offers
