choices.text: The voice laughs, and teaches you a little before it flees into the dark.

choices.label: Sell the bottle at the next city
choices.text: A dealer in forbidden things pays well, and asks no questions.

choices.label: Draw a binding array around the bottle
choices.text: You do not hold the seal with strength, you build it: lines of silver wire, eight stakes, a pattern that will outlast you. The bottle goes quiet for good, and the old sect that guarded it leaves its reward at the array's eye.

encounters.text: A beggar at the market gate has the dying embers of a Nascent Soul behind his eyes. A sect-war cripple, thrown out when his usefulness ended. He looks at your hands, not your face.

choices.label: Give him a core-mending pill
choices.text: He weeps, and bows, and says nothing. Word of your kindness gets around.

choices.label: Toss him a few stones and move on
choices.text: He catches them without looking up.

choices.label: Take his sect's token, he has no use for it
choices.text: The token opens doors in places that do not ask where it came from.

choices.label: Reforge the sect token into a grave-blade
choices.text: You build a fire at the grave and fold the sect's old token into a blade, hammer-stroke by stroke, while the beggar tells you whose it was. He sets the sword on the grave himself, and presses the rest of his old hoard on you.

encounters.text: Two Nascent Soul elders, one righteous and one demonic, trade blows across a ravine. Neither has yet noticed that the fight has been heading for a sleeping spirit-vein.

choices.label: Help the righteous elder
choices.text: The demonic cultivator is driven off and the vein is saved. The elder presses a gift into your hand.

choices.label: Watch from the cliff and learn
choices.text: Two lifetimes of technique unfold below you. You take away only what your eyes can hold.

choices.label: Help the demonic elder
choices.text: The righteous one retreats cursing. Your ally is, in his way, generous.

choices.label: Inscribe a truce talisman between the elders
choices.text: Between two blades you slap down a talisman stroked in a single breath, and the air itself refuses to be cut. Both elders stand panting. When they have remembered their manners, both pay for the lesson.

encounters.text: On the highest peak a storm has been breaking for a thousand years, and never moves. You sit in it for ten days and listen to what the lightning is saying.
Behind a veil of illusion lies a grove no one has harvested in ten thousand years. Spirit herbs grow thick as grass, and the qi beneath them is rich as honey.
A stele on a lonely island is carved with the breathing art of an extinct sect. The sect died, but its stone still remembers, and gives its canon to those who read all of it.
A merchant's mule bolts through the lane, scattering chickens, with its owner wheezing far behind. The rope trails in the dust within easy reach.

choices.label: Catch the mule and return it
choices.text: You grab the rope and walk the sullen beast back. The merchant presses a few stones into your hand and swears you are an honest youth.

choices.label: Follow your luck after the mule
choices.text: The mule drags you down a ditch lane to where a dropped saddlebag has burst open in the mud, full of silver and a few stray stones. The merchant is glad enough of the mule to ask no questions.

on_fail.text: The mule doubles back through a hedge and you chase it down three lanes of mud. By the time you catch it the merchant has found it himself, and you have only scratches and a lost afternoon to show for it.

choices.label: Lead it off and sell it
choices.text: A carter two villages over asks no questions. The coin is good; the merchant's curses fade behind you.

choices.label: Let it run
choices.text: You step aside. The mule thunders on, and the merchant's shouts go with it.

encounters.text: Behind the dyer's shed, a ring of men crouch over dice. A farmer is losing his seed-money, and the house man smiles too widely.

choices.label: Expose the loaded dice
choices.text: You catch the house man's sleeve and the weighted dice roll out. The farmer gets his coin back and the den clears out.

choices.label: Join the house and fleece the farmer
choices.text: You slip the house man a word and take a share of the farmer's last coins.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.text: It is none of your business. You leave the dice rattling behind you.

encounters.text: A filthy beggar holds out a bowl at the well. His hands are grimy, but his eyes, when they meet yours, are far too old and far too clear.

choices.label: Share your food and sit with him
choices.text: He eats slowly, says little, then taps your brow. Warmth sinks into your dantian before he wanders off, humming.

choices.label: Drive him off
choices.text: You shove the bowl away. He shrugs and shuffles out of sight, and the lane feels colder than before.

encounters.text: {villager} and a neighbour shout across a boundary stone, each swearing the damp corner of the field, where spirit grass grows, is theirs. Neither will give way.

choices.label: Judge it fairly and split the grass
choices.text: You walk the old boundary and divide the corner evenly. Both grumble, and both thank you. {villager} leaves a bundle at your feet.

choices.label: Talk both farmers into sharing the corner
choices.text: You hear each out, name the cost of a feud to the harvest and the price of a shared well, and they end by clasping forearms. {villager} swears you will never pay for a bowl of rice in this village again.

choices.label: Side with the one who pays
choices.text: A pinch of stones settles your opinion. The other farmer is left with nothing, and {villager} will not meet your eye.

choices.label: Stay out of it
choices.text: You leave them to shout.

encounters.text: An old herb-gatherer lies against a mossy trunk, a bad fall twisting his leg. He clutches a hide map and gasps that it marks a hidden spring only he knows.

choices.label: Splint his leg and carry him home
choices.text: It costs you the day. At his door he presses the map into your hands. 'The spring keeps no secrets from the kind.'

choices.label: Read the map's smudges with your spirit sense
choices.text: Before he can speak you feel it: the map is a decoy, and the real hollow lies a hundred paces uphill, thick with dew grass. You carry him home, then come back and cut it clean.

choices.label: Take the map and leave him
choices.text: His hand is too weak to hold on. You pocket the map and his pouch, and do not look back.

encounters.text: Following the hide map past a split boulder, you find a small pool ringed with pale herbs, its water faintly warm with spiritual qi.
A travelling recruiter in grey robes sets a crystal on a stool and calls for volunteers. 'Place your hand and we shall see what the heavens gave you.'

choices.label: Test honestly and give back the fee
choices.text: The crystal glows and he nods, writing nothing down. Impressed by your honesty, he tips you a few stones for your trouble.

choices.label: Palm the crystal-fee jar
choices.text: While he turns to the next child, a handful of stones vanishes into your sleeve.

encounters.text: On a switchback below the sect gates, an outer disciple has a thin junior pinned against the rock, shaking out his pouch. 'Tribute,' he sneers. 'Every month, remember?' The junior's eyes find yours.

choices.label: Step in and spar the bully down
choices.text: You catch the bully's wrist and offer him a bout instead. Onlookers gather as he accepts, red-faced.

choices.label: Take a cut of the tribute
choices.text: You lean on the rock and name a price for looking away. The bully grins and counts out your share.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: Sect politics are not your quarrel. Behind you, a pouch rattles empty.

encounters.text: A rag-covered stall hawks 'counterfeit Qi Gathering Pills, honest fakes, one stone apiece!' You turn one in the light. The pill-fire has the clean green gleam of a superior grade: the seller has no idea what he is selling.

choices.label: Buy the whole tray at fake-pill prices
choices.text: You count out a handful of stones and walk away with a tray of superior pills while the seller thanks you for taking his junk.

choices.label: Tell him what he has and buy one fairly
choices.text: He goes pale, then laughs until he cries. He insists on pressing two into your hands for the favour of the truth.

choices.label: Report him to the Pavilion appraisers
choices.text: The Pavilion appraisers confirm the pills, pay you a finder's fee and quietly buy out his stock for themselves.

encounters.text: A silver-furred kit with a faint spirit glimmer mewls under a thorn bush, a snare tight around one paw. Somewhere on the slope above, a mother's cry echoes.

choices.label: Free it and carry it back to its den
choices.text: You cut the snare and follow the cries up the rocks. The vixen watches you coldly, then lowers her head. At the den mouth lie a few things the mountain has given her.

choices.label: Sell the kit to a fur-dealer
choices.text: A dealer in the sect market pays well for spirit beasts and asks nothing. The cries on the slope go unanswered.

choices.label: Leave it to fate
choices.text: Mountains have their own justice. You climb on.

encounters.text: A cellar beneath a wine shop rattles with bone dice, and the stakes are spirit stones. A young disciple is losing his month's allowance, and you can feel faint qi in the dice: someone is cheating.

choices.label: Nudge the dice with your own qi and take the pot
choices.text: A thread of qi, a lucky roll, and a mound of stones slides your way. The house has no proof, and the disciple stares at the table.

choices.label: Call the Pavilion inspectors on the house
choices.text: The inspectors arrive within the hour, weigh the dice, and shut the cellar. The disciple gets his stones back, and the Pavilion remembers who tipped them.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: A fool and his stones are soon parted. You climb back into the street.

encounters.text: A rogue cultivator lies in the rocks, a sword wound through his lung. He clutches a torn strip of hide: half a map. 'The rift... where the sword-light falls. Take it. Do not let them have it.'

choices.label: Stay with him until the end and bury him
choices.text: He dies at dusk. You bury him under a cairn, and the strip of hide, marked with the rift where sword-light falls, goes into your sleeve. Studying it, you grasp a few things about how sword qi bends.

choices.label: Take the map and his purse
choices.text: He stops breathing before you are finished. You take the map fragment and a few stones.

choices.label: Leave him; secrets get people killed
choices.text: You walk on. The wind carries his last words away.

encounters.text: Beside a scorched clearing lies a demonic cultivator, long dead. Crouched over the body is his young disciple, barely at Qi Refining, clutching a sword too large for him. 'Master said the sect would come for him. Please. I have nowhere to go.'

choices.label: Take him to a righteous sect's gate
choices.text: You walk him three days to a mountain gate and vouch for him. He does not look back. The master's bundle is yours to keep.

choices.label: Devour his qi to speed your own cultivation
choices.text: The boy's scream is short. His qi, taught on a demonic art, pours into you thick and bitter, and his master's pouch yields a prize.

choices.label: Leave him to his fate
choices.text: Not your quarrel. You do not turn around.

encounters.text: In a back lane of the market you catch a runner moving crates stamped with a righteous sect's seal. Inside, rare pills are stolen from a sect stores. He sees you see it and does not run: 'Name your price, friend, or name your sect.'

choices.label: Report him to the sect envoys
choices.text: The envoys seize the crates and press a reward into your palm, with their thanks.

choices.label: Take a cut of the haul
choices.text: He shrugs and counts out your share. Pills and stones change hands, and nobody saw a thing.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: Sect thieves and sect thief-takers deserve one another.

choices.label: Read the forged seals and expose the ring
choices.text: A glance at the crate seals is enough: the sect's sigils are copied, and badly, the cinnabar thin and the strokes lifeless. You name every flaw to the envoys, who trace the whole ring on your word and pay you handsomely for it.

encounters.text: A bone-pole hut leans in the fog. Inside, a half-starved herbalist is chained among half-finished corpse puppets, and her eyes beg. The refiner's tools lie within reach, and so does his locked chest.

choices.label: Break her chains and escort her out
choices.text: She leads you to her hidden stash of gratitude: a recipe she once copied for a living.

choices.label: Sell her to a slaver at the market
choices.text: A slaver pays on the spot and asks no questions. The refiner's chest comes open too.

choices.label: Smash the refiner's puppets and free her
choices.text: The half-finished corpses lurch up from their racks as you cut her chains. She slips out through the fog while you hold the door.

choices.label: Slip away
choices.text: The marsh keeps its own dead. Mind your footing.

encounters.text: Poachers have fled an abandoned camp, leaving a caged jade-horned deer. It is a rare spirit beast, still breathing, and its antlers glimmer with medicinal qi.

choices.label: Open the cage and let it go
choices.text: The deer bows low, and a trail of luminous leaves opens before it. Where it stood lies a shed antler.

choices.label: Saw off the antlers and sell the beast
choices.text: A herbalist pays handsomely for fresh antlers and more for the live deer.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.text: You walk past the cage.

choices.label: Tend its wounds and win its trust
choices.text: You speak softly, check the rope burns and feed it a pellet from your sleeve. The deer lets you stroke its flank before the cage door even opens, and leaves a shed antler and a gift at your feet.

encounters.text: A once-proud Foundation cultivator kneels outside a moneylender's, his dantian cracked by a failed breakthrough. He offers you his last treasure, a sealed jade case, to clear his debt before the collectors break his legs.

choices.label: Pay his debt for nothing in return
choices.text: He weeps, and presses the jade case on you anyway: his old recipe, the one thing the moneylender did not take.

choices.label: Buy the case for a pittance, leaving him to the collectors
choices.text: You haggle him down to scraps. The collectors' laughter follows you down the street.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: Every cultivator who climbs leaves someone behind.

encounters.text: The air splits like cloth above the ridge. A dragonling drops out of the rift, rimed in void frost, and fixes its gold eyes on you.
A formation of sword light closes around you. 'The alliance has a ledger of your sins,' says the elder in white. 'Kneel and I will read it to you.'
The sky above the ridge goes the colour of old wine. A figure steps down the moonlight, smiling. 'A Soul Formation cultivator, travelling alone. How generous of heaven.'
Lightning walks the ridge in ranks. Above the highest summit a roc opens wings that blot out the cloud sea, and screams.
A black banner stands in the broken battlefield, and ten thousand faces ripple in its cloth. 'Another soul for the banner,' says the hand that holds it.
The vault door has no handle, only a star-silver eye that opens as you near. The thing behind it has been waiting since before your sect had a name.

A Soul Formation elder sits shackled in a cairn of frozen stone, his own alliance's seals burned into his arms. 'They call me a traitor,' he says. 'I only refused to burn a village. Free me, or leave me, or sell me. I will not beg.'

choices.label: Break the seals and free him
choices.text: The seals scream as they shatter. He bows, once, and presses a jade slip of his life's insight into your hand.

choices.label: Take his storage ring and leave him
choices.text: He watches you go without a word. The ring is heavy.

choices.label: Hand him to the Blood Lotus bounty collectors
choices.text: The collectors pay in blood-pills and good humour. He does not look at you again.

encounters.text: Under the shattered battlefield a spirit vein the thickness of a river is bleeding out through a crack. A little power could seal it for a thousand years, or bleed it dry for yourself.

choices.label: Seal the crack with your own qi
choices.text: You pour yourself into the stone until the vein quiets. The ridge will breathe easier for a thousand years.

choices.label: Drink a little and leave the rest
choices.text: You take what a cultivator can carry and walk away from the rest.

choices.label: Drain the vein dry
choices.text: The stone goes grey and cold as you drink. Somewhere below the ridge, a thousand years of spring will not come.

encounters.text: A gate of white jade stands alone on the ridge, humming. Beyond it there is only more ridge, yet the stone offers bargains in the voices of those you have lost.

choices.label: Lay your hand on the seal and pray for the dead
choices.text: The voices quiet. The gate stays shut, but something in your chest has been eased.

choices.label: Walk around it and say nothing
choices.text: The voices follow for a mile, then thin to wind.

choices.label: Break the seal and take what the voices offer
choices.text: They teach you a killing art of the old war before the gate collapses into dust.

encounters.text: A cairn on the highest ledge faces a sky with no cloud in it. You sit before it for ten days and the silence there teaches you the shape of space itself.
Autumn storms break on the ridge, and a lightning-split pine drops a fruit charged with thunder qi. You swallow what you can and bottle the rest.
After a night of snow, a single lotus has opened on a frozen ledge, its petals ringing faintly in the wind. It will not bloom again until the cold returns. You pick it before the sun can touch it.
On a warm night the undergrowth fills with drifting fireflies, and every spirit herb in the glade lights from within. You gather the brightest, and a purple mushroom beneath them.

encounters.name: Hollow Shrine
encounters.text: Where the mist pools thickest, a hollow tree holds a tiny shrine: a moss-furred clay tablet and a bowl of long-dried offerings, left by some herb-gatherer of an age past. Beneath the tablet, bundles of spirit herb lie wrapped in oilcloth, and a faint warmth of old devotion lingers in the air.

choices.label: Bow to the tablet and move on
choices.text: You bow, tuck the herbs away and leave the shrine as quiet as you found it.

choices.label: Sit a while before the tablet
choices.text: You sit in the old devotion until the mist thins. Something settles in your breathing.

encounters.name: The Founder's Well
encounters.text: Behind the last house, where the lane gives out into weeds, you find a stone well the villagers have stopped drawing from. Its rim is worn smooth by a century of palms, and a clay cup of old rice wine sits on the lip, as if someone had left it for a guest. The water below is strangely still, and faintly cold.

choices.label: Drink from the well
choices.text: The water is sweet and bitingly cold. It settles in your dantian like a seed, and you sit by the rim until the chill becomes warmth.

choices.label: Pour out the wine and leave a stone
choices.text: You pour the wine back into the well and leave a copper behind the cup. An old woman watching from a doorway nods, and presses a handful of dried herbs into your palm.

encounters.name: The Buried Stall
encounters.text: Between two warehouses, where a meteor once split the street, a stall has been swallowed by the crater's lip and left standing. The awning is scorched, the counter fused to glassy stone. Under it, a tin box of unsold goods has survived whatever happened here.

choices.label: Pry open the tin box
choices.text: Inside lie a few shards of star-metal wrapped in rotted silk, worth more than the stall ever earned.

choices.label: Ask the neighbours who kept it
choices.text: A noodle seller remembers the old stallkeeper and sighs. She asks you to take his herbs to be sold and remember his name, and presses a fruit from her own stores into your hand for the trouble.

encounters.name: The Sword Scar
encounters.text: Along a cliff face above the cloud line, a single cut runs straight as a ruled line for a hundred zhang, so clean the rock has not weathered at its edge. Wind sings through it like a struck string. Frost orchids grow in a seam along the lip, where no seed should have taken hold.

choices.label: Read the scar until the light turns
choices.text: You follow the cut with your eyes, again and again, until your breath falls into its rhythm. You come away with a sharper mind and a little more qi in the dantian.

choices.label: Gather the orchids from its edge
choices.text: You lean out over the drop and gather the orchids carefully, leaving the roots. The wind through the scar seems, for a moment, to soften.

encounters.name: The Lantern Cairn
encounters.text: On a hummock of firm ground, someone has stacked white stones into a cairn and hung a rusted lantern from a dead branch above it. The wick is long gone, yet a pale green flame sits in the glass and does not gutter. Around it the marsh mist parts, as though the drowned dead gather here to stand quietly.

choices.label: Say a prayer for the drowned
choices.text: You speak the names you can guess at and the flame brightens gently, then settles. The mist smells of lilies instead of rot, and you leave lighter.

choices.label: Take the lantern's flame oil
choices.text: The glass holds a cold thick oil that smells of grave soil. You decant it, and the flame goes out with a faint sigh. The marsh feels hungrier afterwards.

encounters.name: The Fallen Beast King
encounters.text: On the lee of a ridge the thunder never reaches, the ribs of something enormous arch over a hollow like the roof of a ruined hall. The bone is dark and glassy, still humming with spirit pressure after a thousand years. Orchids have rooted in the marrow channels and are fat with qi.

choices.label: Meditate within the ribcage
choices.text: The old pressure presses down on your shoulders and then lifts, as if the beast acknowledged you. You rise with the whole day's cultivation in a single breath.

choices.label: Harvest the marrow orchids
choices.text: You take the fattest orchids and a vial of marrow-sap, and leave the bones undisturbed.

encounters.text: Children hang riddles from paper lanterns along the riverbank. A grandmother offers a sweet rice cake and a few coins to anyone who can answer one.
A villager presses a blank paper lantern into your hands to float for someone you have lost.

choices.label: Float it for the departed
choices.text: You write a name you have not spoken in years and watch the lantern sail away with the rest. Your heart feels lighter.

choices.label: Pick a pocket in the crowd
choices.text: The crowd is thick and the lanterns dazzle every eye. You lift a fat purse and are gone before the music stops.

encounters.text: You find an overgrown grave no one has tended in years and sweep it clean. The old disciple's lingering gratitude settles over you like warm sunlight.
Rows of offerings lie before the ancestral tablets: wine, fruit and a few spirit stones left for the dead.

choices.label: Add your own stone and bow
choices.text: You leave a single stone and bow three times. The incense seems to burn a little brighter.

choices.label: Chant with the disciples
choices.text: You chant with the disciples until your voice is hoarse. The old sutras clear your mind.

choices.label: Take the stones when no one is looking
choices.text: The dead have no use for spirit stones, you tell yourself. The cold tablets seem to watch you go.

encounters.text: Cultivators gather on a rooftop to compose verses beneath the full moon. Yours earns a round of laughter and a cup of warm wine.
Alone beside a still pool, you watch the moon's reflection until you can no longer tell the water from the sky. The Dao of water brushes your mind.
A stall keeper in a hurry to close shoves a heavy basket of moon cakes at you, then looks away at the crowd.

choices.label: Pay fairly and share them
choices.text: You pay full price and hand the cakes around. A grateful crowd presses small gifts on you.

choices.label: Walk off without paying
choices.text: By the time he turns around you are lost among the lanterns, cakes and all.

encounters.text: A merchant caravan has stopped for the night. The guards wave you to their fire and an old drover shares hot tea; sitting beside it your breathing settles into an easy rhythm.
A mule cart lies on its side across the road, sacks spilled in the dust. Its owner, a wiry old farmer, is pinned by one leg and swearing weakly.

choices.label: Lift the cart and help him reload
choices.text: It costs you half a day, but the farmer's thanks follow you down the road.

choices.label: Take the strongbox under the seat
choices.text: He is in no state to stop you. The strongbox is heavier than it looks, and the farmer's curses fade slowly behind you.

encounters.name: The Explorer's Map
encounters.text: Beneath a cairn of sword-scarred stones you find a wounded explorer clutching a scrap of silk. 'The Sunken Sword Tomb,' he rasps. 'The mists part for it once a decade, but only those who know the way...'

choices.label: Bind his wounds and stay with him
choices.text: You tend him through the night. At dawn he presses the map into your hands with a grateful, shaking smile.

choices.label: Buy the map for 150 spirit stones
choices.text: He haggles weakly, then counts the stones twice and hands over the silk. 'May it lead you better than it led me.'

choices.label: Take it from his dying hand
choices.text: He is too weak to resist. You pocket the silk and leave him to the mountain wind.

choices.label: Leave him to his fate
choices.text: Not your quarrel. You walk on, and the cairn falls behind you.

encounters.text: A scarred man steps out of the roadside brush with a rusty blade. "Toll road," he grins. "Ten stones, or I take it off your corpse."

choices.label: Pay the toll (10 spirit stones)
choices.text: He weighs the coins in his palm and melts back into the brush. You walk on a little lighter.

choices.label: Refuse and fight
choices.text: You set your feet. The highwayman's grin slips.

encounters.text: A small child sits crying on a milestone, a basket of eggs in her lap. She wandered from her caravan and cannot find the way back to her village.

choices.label: Walk her home
choices.text: It takes the better part of a day. Her mother weeps and presses cold dumplings on you; half the village waves you off.

choices.label: Carry her the whole way on your back
choices.text: Her village lies half a day off through heat and mud. You shoulder her and the egg basket without slowing, and by dusk the long walk has loosened something in your breathing. Her mother weeps and presses food on you.

choices.label: Point down the road and move on
choices.text: You give her directions and keep your pace. You hope she finds it.

encounters.text: Three sect disciples in matching robes block the road and ask, politely, for your token and your business. Their hands rest on their sword hilts.

choices.label: Answer honestly and show your hands
choices.text: The leader nods, satisfied. "Travel safely, senior." They step aside.

choices.label: Slip them 20 spirit stones
choices.text: The leader's eyes slide away from your face as the stones vanish. "Move along."

choices.label: Brush past them
choices.text: The leader takes it as an insult and draws.

encounters.text: A cultivator lies against a boulder, robes black with blood. He is already dead. A storage ring glints on his finger, and something small and bitter has been scratched into the stone: a name.

choices.label: Take the ring
choices.text: The ring comes off stiffly. Inside are a few stones and a sealed pill, nothing that would tell you who killed him.

choices.label: Bury him with the ring
choices.text: You dig by hand, in silence, and cut his name on a flat stone. The qi of the road settles around you like a blessing.

encounters.text: A lone beast, bleeding and half-mad, has been driven out of a beast tide far to the east. It spots you across the road and lowers its head.
Last night a falling star struck the road verge. The crater is still warm, and in its heart lies a fist-sized fragment, humming faintly with starlight.
Red-robed figures drop from the cliffs on both sides. "Fellow path," one calls, "but we are short of blood tonight. Your pills, or your life." Their elder steps forward.

A senior on a flying sword slows beside you, silver hair streaming. "You walk too slowly, junior," he says, and flicks a thread of true qi into your dantian. "The mountain pass ahead floods in spring. Go by the high ridge."

A one-armed old soldier leans on the well-sweep and watches you shadow-box in the lane. "Your feet are lying to your fists, youngster," he grunts, and spends five days wrapping your stance in the plain, hard habits of a man who survived three border wars.

Fresh wolf tracks cross the snow in a staggered line. You follow them at a distance and crouch in the white hush, watching the pack run down a deer: the feint, the patient circle, the single clean lunge. You carry the rhythm of it back in your bones.
A lean traveller steps into the middle of the road, shrugs off his pack and grins. "No blood, friend. A bout, for the road's sake. I have walked a hundred li looking for someone who hits back."

choices.label: Accept the bout
choices.text: You trade blows in the dust until one of you finally cannot lift an arm.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.text: He laughs, bows, and lets you pass. "Another day, then."

encounters.text: Below a thin waterfall, two Azure Cloud outer disciples spar barefoot on the wet stones. They wave you closer without breaking rhythm, and for four days you trade corrections with them, learning what only an opponent's hands can teach.

encounters.name: A waterfall's weight
encounters.text: Deep in the mist a waterfall thunders into a black pool, so heavy that the herb-gatherers say it has broken men's backs. Moss-covered stones line the pool, worn smooth by those who tried to stand beneath it.

choices.label: Stand under the waterfall for days
choices.text: The water hammers your shoulders flat and drives the breath from your lungs. By the second day you stop fighting it; by the fifth you stand in it like another stone. You climb out aching, but your bones feel denser.

choices.label: Leave it to the stones
choices.text: You watch the water fall a while, then turn back along the mossy path. Some burdens are better met another day.

encounters.name: A night among the reeds
encounters.text: At dusk the marsh falls silent. The reeds stand motionless and the will-o'-the-wisps hang low over the water like held breaths. An old gatherer once told you that anyone who sits still among them until dawn, without flinching, learns to hear their own spirit.

choices.label: Sit among the reeds until dawn
choices.text: Cold mud seeps through your robe and shapes whisper just past the edge of sight. You do not move. When grey light finally comes the whispering is only wind, and your mind feels washed and sharp.

choices.label: Make camp on higher ground
choices.text: You find a dry mound well away from the lights and sleep with one hand on your blade. Nothing comes for you, and nothing is learned.

encounters.name: A game of weiqi with a blind elder
encounters.text: Behind a noodle stall, a blind old man sits at a weiqi board with an empty seat across from him. "Sit, young one," he says without turning his head. "I cannot see your face, so I will see your mind. No stakes. The stones are enough."

choices.label: Sit and play a game
choices.text: He beats you in forty moves, then patiently lays the board out again and shows where each thought went wrong. By lamplighting you see the board, and a little of the world, more clearly than before.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.text: "Another day, then," the old man says, and sets the first stone down to play against himself.

encounters.text: {rival} descends the steps of the hall with the thunder of a tribulation still clinging to their robes, a golden core turning slow behind the ribs. 'I crossed the lightning first,' {rival} says, loud enough for the whole street. 'Let everyone see how far a rival can fall behind.'

choices.label: Bow and congratulate {rival}
choices.text: You clasp your fists and mean it, mostly. {rival} blinks, thrown off, and mutters that the next climb will be harder. It is almost warmth.

choices.label: Swear to catch up
choices.text: 'Wait for me at the next gate,' you say. The street goes quiet, and the oath settles in your heart like a seed.

choices.label: Answer the boast with a duel
choices.text: You step off the stairs onto packed earth. The crowd scatters to the walls.

encounters.text: Word of a secret realm opening at dusk has drawn you to a cracked stone arch, and {rival} is already there. Only a sliver of the treasure within will be reachable before the arch collapses. {rival} leans on a pillar. 'Share what we find, or settle who goes first. Your choice.'

choices.label: Share the spoils
choices.text: You enter together, back to back, and split what the realm gives up. {rival} keeps the better half of the herbs and does not argue over the rest.

choices.label: Fight for the right to enter first
choices.text: Qi rises on both sides. The arch hums, and the duel begins before it is finished. By the time it ends, the arch has crumbled and the realm is lost to you both.

choices.label: Let {rival} go in alone
choices.text: You sit at the gate and watch the dusk take {rival}. A hard road home, but no blood on your hands.

encounters.text: {rival} is waiting at your gate, pale from sleepless nights. 'You passed the heavenly tribulation that waits for me,' {rival} says. 'Tell me how you survived it. I will remember who answered.'

choices.label: Teach {rival} what you learned
choices.text: You speak until dawn of lightning, of timing, of the moment your will nearly broke. {rival} bows deeply, tears on both cheeks.

choices.label: Mock {rival}'s weakness
choices.text: 'Survive? Perhaps you should not try.' {rival}'s face goes white, then hard, and does not forget.

choices.label: Name your price (200 spirit stones)
choices.text: {rival} counts out two hundred stones with trembling hands and takes the knowledge as a debt, not a gift.

encounters.text: On a windswept peak, {rival} has set a tiny clay stove and two cups, as if the long road had only ever been one slow afternoon. 'A Nascent Soul looks strange in the mirror,' {rival} says, smiling. 'I thought you might want someone to be strange beside.'

choices.label: Sit and compare your Nascent Souls
choices.text: The two tiny infants peer out of your brows and regard each other with great seriousness. You laugh until the tea goes cold, and learn more than a month of seclusion taught.

choices.label: Drink one cup and go
choices.text: The tea is bitter and good. {rival} does not press you, and watches the clouds a long while after you leave.

choices.label: Test your soul against {rival}'s
choices.text: 'Oh, if you insist,' {rival} says, setting the cup down with care. The stove is moved to a safe distance.

encounters.text: A paper crane lands on your shoulder and unfolds in {rival}'s sharp hand: 'Nascent Soul, at last. Meet me on the old dueling ground at dawn, and let the sky see who was the true genius of our generation.' Half the district has already heard.

choices.label: Answer the summons
choices.text: At dawn the ground is ringed with watching cultivators. You step in, and the air thins.

choices.label: Send the crane back, unopened
choices.text: The crane flutters home. Some call it wisdom, some cowardice; {rival} calls it nothing at all, which is worse.

encounters.text: The ancient ruin you have been studying has been stripped overnight, its wards cut with a precision you recognise. A single splinter of {rival}'s sword aura is left in the doorframe, as a signature. The old grudge has learned to wait, and to wear a Nascent Soul.

choices.label: Hunt {rival} down
choices.text: You follow the cold trail to a ridge of black stone. {rival} is waiting, and has been for years.

choices.label: Pay 400 spirit stones to re-seal the ward
choices.text: Craftsmen are paid, wards rewoven, a loss swallowed. {rival} will hear of it and be disappointed that you did not bleed.

choices.label: Let it lie
choices.text: Some ruins are not worth the war. You walk away and do not look back at the splinter.

encounters.text: On a bare shoulder of the mountain, {rival} lies on a cloak with a jug of cheap wine, watching the stars turn. 'We were two mortals shivering on the same road, once,' {rival} says. 'Now the sky itself leans close to listen. Lie down. Nobody else alive would understand what I am about to say.'

choices.label: Lie down and talk until dawn
choices.text: You trade the fears of three decades: the failed breakthroughs, the funerals, the thinning of the old names. By dawn neither of you has solved anything, and both of you feel lighter.

choices.label: Share one jug and walk on
choices.text: The wine is rough and the company is not. {rival} lifts the jug to your back as you go.

choices.label: Ask {rival} to spar beneath the stars
choices.text: 'Of course,' {rival} says, rising with a grin. 'It is the only way either of us says anything true.'

encounters.text: {rival}'s voice rolls across the wasteland, pressed into every grain of wind: 'Soul Formation, and still you walk the same sky as me. One of us is too many. Come to the broken gate at sunset.' Lesser cultivators have already begun to gather at a safe distance, and to wager.

choices.label: Walk to the broken gate
choices.text: The dust parts around you as you arrive. {rival} stands waiting in the red light, and the watchers forget to breathe.

choices.label: Answer the wind: 'Another day'
choices.text: Your reply carries as far as the gate and no farther. {rival} takes the delay as an insult; the watchers take it as news.

encounters.text: The old war memorial you tend, a cairn for the nameless dead of a forgotten war, has been toppled stone by stone. {rival}'s sword aura lingers in the dust, patient as a tax collector. The grudge has outlived mortal lifetimes, and it has never once forgotten your name.

choices.label: Track {rival} to the end of the world
choices.text: The trail runs to a cliff over a sea of cloud. {rival} is sitting at its edge, and has been for a very long time.

choices.label: Pay 1500 spirit stones to raise the cairn anew
choices.text: Masons are hired, the names recut deeper than before. {rival} will hear of it and wonder, briefly, whether the grudge is still the whole of you.

choices.label: Set the stones back by hand
choices.text: You work through the night without a spell. The dead do not thank you, but the cairn stands, and you sleep.

encounters.text: {rival} stands in the middle of an empty field with one hand raised, and the air before them has a seam in it, thin as a held breath. 'I can only keep it open for the length of a cup of tea,' {rival} says, not turning. 'I have been practicing alone for years. Come and look through it with me.'

choices.label: Stand beside {rival} and look through
choices.text: Beyond the seam there is nothing, and the nothing has a grain, like old wood. You watch it together without speaking until the seam closes, and both of you understand a little more of the door.

choices.label: Nod, and leave {rival} to the work
choices.text: Some doors are opened alone. {rival} does not look away from the seam, but the shoulders loosen a little as you go.

choices.label: Ask {rival} to spar at the edge of the void
choices.text: 'Carefully,' {rival} says, closing the seam with two fingers and turning, grinning at last. 'The field is not that large.'

encounters.text: The sky above you folds open for a moment and {rival}'s voice steps through it: 'Void Refinement, and you still stand where I can find you. The heavens have room for one of us at the top of this generation. Come to the place where the sky is thinnest, and let it decide.' Somewhere far below, mortals look up and wonder at the sound.

choices.label: Step through the fold to {rival}
choices.text: The space closes behind you like a book. {rival} waits on a plain of white stone, robes unmoving in a wind that does not exist.

choices.label: Close the fold with a wave
choices.text: The seam seals itself with a sound like a sheet of silk tearing. {rival} will not forget being shut out, and neither will the sky.

encounters.text: The void-vault you have kept for decades, a pocket of folded space where you stored what the years could not be trusted with, has been cut open from the inside. Nothing is missing but one small token, and in its place hangs a splinter of {rival}'s sword aura. The grudge has learned to walk through walls that are not there.

choices.label: Follow the cut to {rival}
choices.text: The wound in space leads to a cold ledge between two stars of the lower sky. {rival} is sitting there with the stolen token in one palm, as if the grudge had always been the only company worth keeping.

choices.label: Pay 8000 spirit stones to have the vault re-folded
choices.text: Void-smiths are paid, the walls drawn back together thicker than before. {rival} will hear of it, and wonder briefly if you have finally learned to let a thing go.

choices.label: Leave the vault open and walk away
choices.text: You let the empty pocket stand, a small door to nowhere. It is lighter to carry less, and you do not need to see the splinter again.

encounters.text: Below the sect's terraces a young disciple lies curled in the pine needles, lips blue, a dart of black thorn still in the shoulder. The meridians are rotting from the wound outward. Only a proper meridian-mending pill could save them in time; the sect infirmary is half a day away.

choices.label: Feed them a Meridian Mending Pill
choices.text: You press the pill between their lips and guide the medicine along the ruined channels. By dusk the blue has left their mouth, and they weep a thank-you into the needles.

choices.label: Carry them to the infirmary
choices.text: You run the whole way with the junior over your shoulder. They live, though the infirmary elder grumbles that you were slow.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: A sect disciple's troubles are the sect's to solve. The pines hide the shape behind you.

encounters.text: In the doorway of a closed shop sits a gaunt old man in patched robes, an inkstone and a stack of formation sketches on his knees. 'Debts,' he says, without looking up. 'A hundred stones, and the moneylenders take my last copy of the Five Element Gathering Array. I would rather give it to someone who will use it.'

choices.label: Pay his debt (100 spirit stones)
choices.text: You count out the stones. The old man's hands shake as he copies out the array in full, margin notes and all, and presses the sheets into your palm.

choices.label: Buy the sketches for a fair price (30 spirit stones)
choices.text: You haggle him up to thirty. The sketches are crumpled, but the old man's eyes are grateful.

choices.label: Leave him to the moneylenders
choices.text: The moneylenders will have him by nightfall. You pretend not to hear the coughing behind you.

encounters.text: Mist gathers around a leaning grave marker and takes the shape of a drowned woman, hands cupped in the air. She does not threaten; she only points at the azure crystal glinting in your pack, and waits. The reeds have gone quiet. Something has been waiting a long time here for an offering.

choices.label: Offer an Azure Crystal
choices.text: You set the crystal on the grave. The ghost bows, and the mist coils into your dantian like a warm breath. When it clears, the grave is bare and the air feels like a held note.

choices.label: Chant a rite of rest instead
choices.text: You speak the old words until your voice is gone. The mist loosens slowly, and the ghost fades without taking anything.

choices.label: Back away
choices.text: You retreat step by step. The ghost watches you go, hands still cupped.

encounters.text: A sunken study rises from the black water, its roof tiles green with age. A drowned scholar's shade sits at a desk of rotten wood, ink still wet on a scroll about the nature of water. 'Fifty years I have lacked one frost jade salve to seal my last page,' the shade murmurs. 'Spare one, and I will leave you what the page says.'

choices.label: Give a Frost Jade Salve
choices.text: You smear the salve along the scroll's edge. The ink drinks it, the last line completes, and the shade bows. When you read the page, the swamp's slow patience settles into your bones.

choices.label: Read the scroll over the shade's shoulder
choices.text: You catch half a lesson before the shade notices and the water closes over the desk. The half you got is still worth the wet boots.

choices.label: Leave the study to the water
choices.text: Some scrolls are better left to drown. The roof sinks behind you with hardly a ripple.

encounters.text: A hermit smith's forge glows on a cold ledge, its hearth failing for lack of proper fuel. 'My bellows eat spirit stones now,' the old man grumbles, a hammer in a shaking hand. 'Feed the fire three hundred, and I will show you the stroke my master gave me: the one that sets a technique into the arm.'

choices.label: Feed the forge 300 spirit stones
choices.text: The hearth roars blue. For a day and a night the old smith drives you through one stroke, over and over, until your technique moves a half-beat before you think it.

choices.label: Work the bellows for a day
choices.text: Your arms ache and your robe is ruined. The old smith shows you a plain trick of the wrist in return, and says nothing more.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: A forge that cannot pay for its own fuel will not teach you much. The ledge falls quiet behind you.

encounters.text: A great spirit beast lies on her side in the grass, breathing shallowly, three cubs pressed against her belly. Her core is guttering. She cannot speak, but her eyes follow the golden core lotus seed in your pack, and she does not look away.

choices.label: Feed her a Golden Core Lotus Seed
choices.text: She swallows the seed, and her core steadies. She noses each cub toward you in turn, and presses her great brow to your chest before she leaves. Something of her endurance stays with you.

choices.label: Guard the cubs until she wakes
choices.text: You sit with the little ones through the night. By dawn she is on her feet again, weak but alive, and she lets you go with a low rumble.

choices.label: Take a cub's tooth and go
choices.text: The mother cannot lift her head to stop you. The memory is worth less than you hoped.

encounters.text: The sky over the ridge peels open like wet paper. A wyrm slides out of the seam, and the seam does not close behind it.
The road folds shut behind you, and a man in white stands where the horizon used to be. 'The tribunal has read your ledger,' says the censor. 'Confess, and I may let you keep your cultivation.'
The marsh mist goes still, and a village appears in the stranger's open sleeve, tiny lamps still burning. 'A Void Refinement cultivator,' he says warmly. 'You will keep them company.'
A fallen star cracks across the dusk and the roc rides its tail down, thunder streaming off its wings. The world is small to you now; it is not small to the roc.
A door hangs open in the air above the broken wall, and behind it is an empty hall a thousand years deep. 'Company,' says the lord inside, with terrible gentleness. 'At last.'
The breach in the sky above the ruin is still held shut by something that never stopped holding. Its star-silver head turns, and the order it was given ten thousand years ago has not changed.

A thousand mortals huddle in a field that has no sky above it, spilled out of a pocket world that is closing. Their elder looks up at you and does not ask for anything. 'We only wish to know if the ground here is real,' she says.

choices.label: Open a stable gate and carry them out
choices.text: It takes all your qi and most of a month. When the last child steps through, the elder bows until her forehead touches the earth.

choices.label: Sell them a way out for what they carry
choices.text: They hand over every coin and heirloom without a word. You do carry them out; the elder will not look at you.

choices.label: Collapse the world and take what spills out
choices.text: The pocket world folds into your palm like a leaf, and its treasure with it. The silence afterward is very large.

encounters.text: A tomb floats among the ruins, its door sealed by an emperor who once ruled the sky and was not good at sharing. A voice inside offers a bargain: his legacy for a name to carry on.

choices.label: Take his name and tend the tomb
choices.text: You swear to carry the name and keep the offering lamps lit. The emperor's thanks arrives as a single drop of insight.

choices.label: Cut the seals and loot the tomb
choices.text: The emperor's curses are impressive, and brief. His treasury is not.

choices.label: Offer the emperor's soul to a Blood Lotus buyer
choices.text: The buyer pays in blood-pills and does not ask what the screaming was.

encounters.text: An ancient sect keeps a single hall on a single peak, five disciples and one patriarch at Void Refinement who has not slept since the founder died. He asks whether you will guard their gate for a month, or whether you came for what the gate guards.

choices.label: Guard the gate for a month
choices.text: The month is quiet, which is the point. The patriarch finally sleeps, and wakes to find his disciples held the gate without him.

choices.label: Ask only to share the mountain's qi
choices.text: He nods, relieved to have asked and been refused nothing.

choices.label: Take the hall's treasury by force
choices.text: Five disciples scream and one old man does not. The hall is empty when you leave.

encounters.text: On a ledge no road reaches you find a place where the world holds perfectly still. You sit there fifteen days, and the world, small now, turns itself over in your hands.

A bronze bell the size of a house hangs in a sunken temple, its tongue wrapped in reed-rope. A drowned monk sits beneath it, patient as a stone. 'Three hundred years I have wanted to ring it once, and cannot lift the rope,' he says. 'A soul infant fruit would let my ghost rise, if you carry one. In return I would ring you the tone I learned in life.'

choices.label: Give a Soul Infant Fruit
choices.text: The monk eats the fruit's glow and rises, light as steam. He takes the rope and rings once, and the tone goes through your Nascent Soul like warm rain, unlocking a patience you had not known you lacked.

choices.label: Lift the rope for him
choices.text: It takes all your strength and half a day. The bell sounds a single flat note, and the monk's ghost bows, unrisen but content.

choices.label: Wade out of the temple
choices.text: The bell hangs silent over the black water behind you.

encounters.text: A stone warden of the old sect stands in a collapsed hall, its eyes dim, its fist closed over a stele it was set to guard. When you near, its mouth grinds open: 'The stroke carved here costs five thousand spirit stones in offering to the sect's long-dead treasury. I was told to ask. I was not told to stop asking.'

choices.label: Lay down 5000 spirit stones
choices.text: The warden counts every stone into a crevice in its chest, and its fist opens. The stele's stroke is carved deep; you trace it for a day and a night, and your technique moves as if you had practised it for a month.

choices.label: Trace the stele through the warden's fingers
choices.text: You read what its fist lets slip and take away the first third of the stroke. The warden's eyes stay dim.

choices.label: Leave the hall
choices.text: The warden keeps asking long after you have gone.

encounters.text: Beneath the lamp-lit towers a thousand refugees from a burned mountain sect crowd a collapsing warehouse. A grey-haired elder bows to you in the old way. 'A hall to house them costs four thousand spirit stones and a name the city's guilds will listen to,' she says. 'Lend us both, Nascent Soul elder, and the whole market will know who stood up.'

choices.label: Fund the hall with 4000 spirit stones
choices.text: You sign the deed in your own name. By the end of the month there are roofs and rice, and the guilds say your name in the market as people say the name of a good neighbour.

choices.label: Vouch for them with the guilds
choices.text: A word from a cultivator of your standing shifts a few stubborn merchants. They get a floor and a roof for the winter, not a hall.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: There are always refugees. The lamps are very bright tonight.

encounters.text: The ridge breathes. What you took for a hill turns, and a valley with rivers and small lamps shifts in its flank as the behemoth lifts its head.
The arbiter steps out of the air as if out of his own skin. 'Whole men have nothing to hide,' he says. 'Show me you are whole.'
A throne of grown bone rises out of the marsh mud, and the ancestor on it smiles with teeth that are not all his own. 'Come closer. I am too old to walk to you.'
A heartbeat rolls over the peaks, slow and enormous, and the vermilion roc comes down on it. The sky keeps its time, and you are not part of the song.
The ruined hall fills with courtiers made of bone, bowing in rows. At the far end the sovereign rises from himself. 'Welcome back,' he says, and means it for someone else.
A door has stood shut here since the vow was made, and a colossus of star silver stands before it. It does not know its maker is dust; it only knows you are not him.
A god's body lies half-sunk in the marsh, long as a river and cold as a river, its heart still beating once a day. Fisherfolk have built a village on its ribs and ask you, politely, not to wake it.

choices.label: Listen to the heart for ten days
choices.text: Your own pulse slows to match it, and flesh and void stop quarrelling for a while. The fisherfolk bring you tea.

choices.label: Pay 60000 spirit stones to bury the heart in stone
choices.text: The village is spared the dreams. The god is spared nothing, and you carry the weight of it away.

choices.label: Cut out the heart
choices.text: The village sinks by morning. The heart is warm in your hands and does not stop beating.

encounters.text: A stern figure sits on the mountain road, a scale in each hand. 'Every cultivator who passes weighs their body against the world they have taken,' it says. 'Step on, or be weighed.'

choices.label: Let yourself be weighed
choices.text: One scale falls and the other rises. It does not tell you which is you.

choices.label: Break the scales
choices.text: The judge stands, and the mountain stands with it.

choices.label: Slip a hand into the judge's sleeve
choices.text: It lets you take the purse. It writes your name down in a book that is already very long.

encounters.text: A bone clerk waves you into a court whose sovereign is absent, and slides a petition across the table: a ghost wants her body back from the soil it has become.

choices.label: Raise the body from the soil
choices.text: It takes a month of qi and a very patient spell. She thanks you without turning around.

choices.label: Dismiss the petition and take the clerk's fees
choices.text: The clerk blinks, once, and the fees are heavy in your sleeve.

choices.label: Bind the ghost to your own body
choices.text: She screams, and then, much worse, stops. Your flesh is warmer than it was.

encounters.name: The Abandoned Herb Cache
encounters.text: Under a fallen cedar, wrapped in oilcloth gone green with damp, lies a herb-picker's cache: bundles of dew grass and spirit herb, tied and labelled in a careful hand. A tally-stick leans beside it. Whoever stored it has not come back for a long time, or perhaps never will.

choices.label: Take only a fair share and leave a mark for the owner
choices.text: You take a few bundles, notch the tally-stick with what you took and tie a strip of cloth to the cedar. If the picker returns, they will know someone was honest.

choices.label: Take it all
choices.text: Every bundle goes into your pack, oilcloth and all. The cedar looks very bare behind you.

choices.label: Leave it untouched
choices.text: A picker's winter stores are not yours to count. You settle the oilcloth back over the bundles and walk on.

encounters.name: The Old Alchemist's Notes
encounters.text: A hollow stump holds a waxed satchel, and in it a sheaf of notes in a cramped, faded hand: furnace temperatures, drying times, the weight of each herb down to the grain. The last page is a formula for mending the organs after a hard blow, half scratched out, as if the writer lost patience with it.

choices.label: Puzzle out the scratched-out formula
choices.text: You read the margins until the crossings-out make sense: he was right the first time and only distrusted his own furnace. You copy the Visceral Mending Pill cleanly into your own notes.

on_fail.text: You squint at the margins until dusk, and the crossings-out refuse to make sense. A damp wind takes the loose pages, and the formula goes with them.

choices.label: Sell the notes in the village
choices.text: A herb-seller gives you stones for the satchel without reading past the first page.

choices.label: Burn the notes for warmth
choices.text: You do not trust a dead stranger's furnace. The pages curl and blacken, and the secret goes up with the smoke.

encounters.name: The Broken Forge
encounters.text: At the edge of the village stands a smithy with its bellows split down the middle and its hearth cold. Iron lumps sit forgotten in the ashes. The smith's widow watches from the doorway, wondering aloud whether anyone knows how to make the old thing breathe again.

choices.label: Patch the bellows and relight the hearth
choices.text: You cut a new leather bellows-skin, seal the seams with resin and coax the coals alive. The widow presses a share of the iron on you, and the village gets its forge back.

choices.label: Rake the iron from the ashes and go
choices.text: The widow is too tired to stop you. You leave with the best of the lumps and her eyes on your back.

choices.label: Leave the forge as you found it
choices.text: Some things are not yours to mend. The widow nods as though she expected nothing else.

encounters.text: The mountain lifts a leg. A country of lamplit towns sways on its back as the tortoise turns one eye toward you.
The magistrate unfolds from a fold in the air, sleeves heavy with names. 'A great vehicle carries many,' he says. 'Show me who rides with you.'
A throne of black jade settles into the mud, and then another beyond it, and another. On every one the same ancestor smiles. 'Sit,' he says, from all of them.
A shadow crosses the valley and does not finish crossing. High above, a peng folds its wings and dives, and the thunder behind it comes later.
The hall opens onto a sky made of the dead, tier on tier, all kneeling. The sovereign on the highest tier lowers his hand. 'Kneel, and be counted.'
A gate of star silver stands open on nothing, and its guardian stands in the doorway. It does not stop you leaving. It only forbids what you came to do.
The clouds above the ridge stop moving. Beneath them a tortoise rises with a storm folded into every plate, and the first thunder rolls out of its shell.
A warden in plain grey stands on a stair that is not there. "You are close," he says. "Show me what you would leave behind."
The lightning over the marsh strikes the same spot nine times and finds no one. Then an old man steps out of the ninth flash, yawning. "Ah. Company."
Where the storm is thickest a dark shape banks and feeds, swallowing bolts whole. It turns its head, and the next bolt is yours.
A hall of scorched glass, and in it a throne heaped with shards of failed tribulations. The sovereign smiles. "Everyone pays in the end. Let us see your sum."
A stair of star silver climbs into cloud, and a guardian stands on its first step. It does not stop you leaving. It only asks if you are finished below.
A bronze bell hangs from a dead pine on a ridge where the lightning has struck so often the rock has turned to glass. It rings on its own, once, whenever a cultivator somewhere fails the last step.

choices.label: Ring it back with a steady heart
choices.text: You answer the bell with one clear stroke and hold it until the echo stills. The sky stops listening for a failure, and something in your Dao hears thunder as a teacher.

choices.label: Pay 500000 spirit stones to still the bell for the fallen
choices.text: The stones melt into the bronze and the bell goes quiet for a season. The sky seems to owe you a small, grave courtesy.

choices.label: Strike it to call the lightning down, and gather what falls
choices.text: The bell screams and the sky answers. You stand in the glass-fire and carry off what the bolt leaves behind, with the sky's attention on your back.

encounters.text: A cairn of fused stone stands where a cultivator's last tribulation ended. Ash still lies in its shadow, and a little of the dead one's will, unfinished, clings to whoever stops here.

choices.label: Speak their name and give the ash your own qi to rest on
choices.text: You pour a long breath of cultivation into the ash and name the one who fell. The wind carries it up, and your own road feels less lonely.

choices.label: Raise the cairn higher for 450000 spirit stones
choices.text: Masons and stones both are hired from the nearest town, and the cairn grows a tier before you leave. No one thanks you, which is how such work should be.

choices.label: Break the cairn open and take what the dead one carried
choices.text: Under the stone lies a satchel the lightning forgot. You do not look at the ash as you shoulder it.

encounters.text: An old monster sits in a ruin with its roof torn off, calmly watching the clouds. 'My lightning is overdue,' he says. 'It has been overdue for three thousand years. I would like it to find someone else first.'

choices.label: Walk him to a deep cave and keep watch until the clouds pass
choices.text: It takes six days and all your patience. When the sky gives up and leaves, he bows to you with the stiff grace of a man who has not bowed in an age.

choices.label: Sell him a lightning-proof charm for 350000 spirit stones
choices.text: He pays in coin from three different dynasties and does not haggle. You both pretend the charm will work.

choices.label: Push him out beneath the open sky
choices.text: He sighs as though he expected it. The lightning, long overdue, arrives at once, and something old and hungry comes out of it to look for you.

encounters.text: A lamp burns on a bare ridge with no one to tend it. Each flicker is a vow someone swore and did not keep, and the flame leans toward you as toward an old debtor.

choices.label: Hold the flame in a steady heart
choices.text: You keep it company through a night of other people's regrets. By dawn it burns straight, and something in your Dao burns straight with it.

choices.label: Feed the lamp 400000 spirit stones so the vows may be paid
choices.text: The stones burn white and the oaths go out one by one, forgiven. The lamp thanks you by dimming, and your own vows weigh less.

choices.label: Drink the lamp's oil
choices.text: Every broken promise runs down your throat like fire. You will keep none of them, and neither will the lamp.

encounters.text: A ferryman poles a skiff across a river of pale light that flows up the mountainside. 'Few come this far on foot,' he says. 'The fare is whatever you cannot carry across.'

choices.label: Pay the fare in qi
choices.text: He takes a slow draught of your cultivation and ferries you to the far bank and back. The water remembers you kindly.

choices.label: Pay the fare in stones, and ride in silence
choices.text: Three hundred thousand stones go into the water, and the ferryman asks nothing more. The crossing is quiet, and the quiet is worth something.

choices.label: Take the pole and throw the ferryman in
choices.text: He goes under without protest and a shape in the water stirs. When you reach the bank the skiff is yours and full of what he never spent.

encounters.text: An old cultivator sits cross-legged before an unopened gate, his beard grown through the floor. 'I could have gone ten thousand years ago,' he says without turning. 'There was one more thing to see. Sit. Ask me whether it was worth it.'

choices.label: Sit and ask
choices.text: He talks for a month of what the end of the road is made of. You leave with his regrets and a better understanding of your own.

choices.label: Leave an offering of 350000 spirit stones at his knee
choices.text: He does not open his eyes. The stones are gone when you look back, and the road is lighter.

choices.label: Take the seat before his gate
choices.text: The old man laughs once, a dry sound, and rises to stop you. 'Then you may have it,' he says, 'when I am done with you.'

encounters.text: A peddler sits on a roadside rock with a satchel of yellow paper, fanning himself with a ruined sheet. "Blank talisman paper, cinnabar-ready," he says. "Cheaper than the market, and no questions about who is asking."

choices.label: Buy a bundle
choices.text: Eight stones change hands and five clean sheets go into your sleeve. The peddler tips an imaginary hat and settles back to his fanning.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: You shake your head. He shrugs and calls the same offer to the next dust cloud on the road.

encounters.text: An old man kneels at an ancient milestone, chipping lichen from its face with a bent chisel. The script on it is older than the village road, and his hands shake more than the work allows.

choices.label: Help him
choices.text: You hold the stone steady and clear the lichen with him until dusk. He says little, but he presses a warm rice cake into your hand.

choices.label: Read the old script
choices.text: The strokes are older than any sect's, and as you follow them your breath falls in step with their rhythm. When you look up the old man is smiling at you.

encounters.text: Rain comes down in sheets and you duck under the roof of a wayside shrine. A travelling alchemist is already there, wringing out his sleeves beside a small clay stove.

choices.label: Share his fire and talk until it clears
choices.text: He trades road stories for yours, and when the clouds break he presses a Spirit Herb into your hand. "For the company," he says.

choices.label: Ask him for a pill
choices.text: He eyes you, laughs, and tosses you a Qi Gathering Pill from his belt. "A small thing. Remember the old man at the shrine when you are great."

encounters.text: Behind the headman's barn his grandson and three other boys are pounding a sandbag and bruising each other's forearms. "Come on, stranger," the boy calls, wiping his nose. "Show us how a cultivator stands."

choices.label: Spar with the boys for a few days
choices.text: You trade slow, careful blows with them until the sand is in your teeth and the stance finally settles under you.

choices.label: Break their sandbag post with one blow
choices.text: You plant your feet, breathe out, and strike. The post cracks through and the boys fall silent, then crowd round begging to see it again. You spend ten days drilling it with them.

choices.label: Buy the boys a round of sweet cakes
choices.text: They cheer, and the headman's wife slips a few stones into your hand for 'keeping them out of trouble'.

encounters.text: A grey-bearded hunter crouches over a patch of torn earth, tracing the claw marks with his thumb. "Wolf, and a big one. See how it dug in before the lunge? If you must walk these woods, learn to read that."

choices.label: Ask him to show you how a wolf lunges
choices.text: He plays the wolf with a stick and you the prey, over and over, until your feet know when to give ground and when to strike.

choices.label: Read the sign yourself and answer his test
choices.text: You study the marks, name the wolf's weak side, and the old hunter grunts, impressed. He spends ten days drilling you in turning a lunge aside.

on_fail.text: You name the wrong side, and the old hunter laughs and shows you the right one with a stick across your shins. It is still a lesson, though a short and sore one.

choices.label: Help him carry his pelts to the road
choices.text: The bundle is heavy and smells of the forest. At the road he presses two stones into your hand and a word of thanks.

encounters.text: A tired young man in an outer disciple's grey robe is sitting on the well's rim with a bucket between his boots. "Fourth day of latrine duty and the steward wants the herb beds weeded by dusk," he says. "You look like you have an afternoon to spare. Sect rules say nobody checks who does it, as long as it is done."

choices.label: Weed the herb beds for him
choices.text: You spend three days on your knees in the dirt. He is so grateful he tells the whole village, and the headman nods at you in the lane afterwards.

choices.label: Ask a few stones for the trouble
choices.text: He grimaces, counts out his pay, and hands it over without meeting your eyes. The weeding is done by dusk, and the village hears who charged for it.

choices.label: Wish him luck and move on
choices.text: He sighs, picks up the bucket, and trudges off toward the beds.

encounters.name: The Cart in the Ford
encounters.text: A merchant's cart has dropped a wheel into the river ford below the village, its ox lowing, the bales on the bed already darkening with spray. The merchant wades round it in despair. "Another hour and the current takes the lot," he calls. "Two backs would move it. One strong back, perhaps."

choices.label: Help him unload and haul it out
choices.text: You spend the day knee-deep in cold water, passing bales hand to hand to the bank. The merchant tells the village who saved his silk, and the ferryman nods to you for a month.

choices.label: Lift the cart out alone
choices.text: You set your shoulders under the axle and heave. The wheel grinds free of the mud and the ox lurches ashore, bales and all. The merchant stares, then counts out stones with shaking hands.

on_fail.text: The axle will not budge and the current drags your feet from under you. By the time the ferrymen come with ropes, the day is gone and you are soaked to the bone.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: It is not your silk. Behind you, the merchant starts wading for the ferrymen.

encounters.name: The Senior's Test
encounters.text: In the village square an Azure Cloud senior in a pressed grey robe has drawn a ring in the dust and is looking over the young cultivators of the village like a buyer at a horse fair. "Outer disciples or not," he says, "I do not care. Anyone who thinks they have a Qi Refining fist, step in. No bones broken, no blood drawn. Stones for whoever lasts."

choices.label: Step into the ring
choices.text: He bows, and for three rounds the dust of the square rises round the two of you. He fights like a man who has done this a hundred times and wants to see what you will do about it. If you wear a sect's robe, he notes your name for its ledger.

choices.label: Watch from the edge of the square
choices.text: You study how the senior turns his hip and drops his guard a hair before each feint. It is not a lesson he meant to give.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: You shake your head and step back. The senior's eyes slide past you to the next face.

encounters.text: An old man with knuckles like walnuts is working a post by the threshing floor, shirt off in the cold. He grins when he sees you. "A cultivator. Humour an old caravan guard: three rounds, no killing. If you stay on your feet I will pay you in herbs from my garden."

choices.label: Spar with the old boxer
choices.text: He hits like a mule and moves like a cat, and for three rounds you trade blows over the frozen dirt.

choices.label: Watch him work the post instead
choices.text: You sit on a barrel and study how he turns his hip into each blow. It is a small thing, but you carry it away.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.text: He shrugs and goes back to his post. "Everybody young is busy," he says to the post.

encounters.name: The Spilled Basket
encounters.text: By a mist-slick stream an old herb-picker kneels over a split basket, its morning's catch of pale grass floating off downstream. Her hands are too stiff to chase it, and she is counting the blades that remain with a sinking face.

choices.label: Wade in and help her gather it
choices.text: You spend the day knee-deep in cold water, fishing the blades out one by one. She presses a bundle of Qi Condensing Grass on you and tells the Qingshi stalls who helped her.

choices.label: Help her, and keep a share for yourself
choices.text: You gather the grass and quietly slip a good handful into your sleeve. She counts her bundle twice and says nothing, which is worse.

choices.label: Leave her to it
choices.text: It is her basket and her stream. You walk on, and the grass drifts out of sight.

encounters.name: The Snared Wolf Cub
encounters.text: A grey wolf cub lies in a hunter's snare, whimpering, one paw bloodied by the wire. Mist wolves hunt in packs, and somewhere in the fog a dam is calling. A beast cultivator would tell you a freed cub remembers for years, and so does a skinned one.

choices.label: Cut the wire and set it free
choices.text: You hold it down with your sleeve and cut the snare away. It bolts into the mist, and from the dark behind it comes a single low howl that does not sound like a threat.

choices.label: Skin the cub and sell the pelt
choices.text: It is quickly done, and you do not look at it afterwards. The pelt is soft and grey and worth more than the mercy would have been.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: You leave the cub to the hunter and the dam. Its whimpering follows you for a long time.

encounters.name: The Salt Caravan
encounters.text: A salt caravan has halted at the roadside, its master pacing beside the lead cart. "Bandits work the next stretch," he says, eyeing your stance. "Walk beside my wagons until the hills end and there are stones in it for you."

choices.label: Guard the caravan
choices.text: You walk the hills beside the wagons. When the raiders come down from the rocks, you are the one they find waiting.

choices.label: Wish them well
choices.text: The master shrugs and clicks his tongue at the oxen. The wagons creak on without you.

encounters.name: The Fallen Rogue
encounters.text: Crows wheel over a ditch beside the road. A rogue cultivator lies there on his back, robes torn, his satchel still strapped across his chest. No one has come for him, and by the look of the crows, no one will.

choices.label: Bury him
choices.text: You dig with a broken stone until dusk and lay him under a cairn. The crows scatter and the satchel is yours, which he would not have begrudged a fellow wanderer.

choices.label: Take the satchel and walk on
choices.text: You cut the strap, weigh it in your hand and leave him to the crows. The road does not hold grudges, only debts.

choices.label: Leave him
choices.text: Not your dead, not your road. You step around the ditch and do not look back at the crows.

encounters.name: The Elder's Carriage
encounters.text: A lacquered carriage with no horses, drawn by two stiff paper oxen, stops in the lane and the whole village goes quiet. The man who steps down wears plain grey and walks as if the ground were something he had agreed to. A Foundation Establishment elder, here to buy rice and rest his bones, with a heavy trunk and no one to carry it.

choices.label: Offer to carry his baggage
choices.text: You shoulder the trunk and walk it to the inn without a word. He studies you over his shoulder, then presses a small pill into your palm. "For the weight," he says, and does not explain.

choices.label: Ask him how Foundation is built
choices.text: You bow and ask your question plainly. His eyes sharpen. "Qi is a river," he says, "and Foundation is the bed you dig for it. Do not hurry the digging." Something in the words unlocks a knot you had not known was there, and you sit at the roadside for a night turning it over.

choices.label: Step aside and let the carriage pass
choices.text: You keep your eyes lowered until the paper oxen have clattered by. Some doors are not yours to knock on yet.

encounters.name: The Hunted Fox
encounters.text: A white fox with two tails drags itself into your path, one hind leg dark with blood, nine-tenths spent. Behind it, through the fog, come the shouts of hunters and the bay of hounds. The fox looks at you with eyes far too old for its size.

choices.label: Hide the fox and face the hunters
choices.text: You tuck the fox into a hollow log and step into the path. The hunters do not believe you when you say you saw nothing, and they have come armed.

choices.label: Hand it over to the hunters
choices.text: You point. The hunters whoop, drop twelve spirit stones into your hand and drag the fox away by the scruff. It does not struggle. It only looks back at you once.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: You step off the path and let the fog close behind you. The hounds' voices pass and fade, and you never learn how it ended.

encounters.name: The Lantern Trail
encounters.text: Pale lanterns hang from the branches in a line no woodcutter hung, each one lit from within by a drop of someone's stray qi. They lead deeper into the mist than any path you have walked, and they gutter as you hesitate.

choices.label: Follow them to the end
choices.text: The trail ends at a moss-bound stone seat where a long-dead cultivator sat out his last winter. You sit where he sat, and his unspent breath settles into your dantian.

choices.label: Snuff the lanterns and take their wicks
choices.text: The wicks are spirit-oil cotton, still faintly warm. A shopkeeper will pay for them; the forest grows a little darker behind you.

choices.label: Read the trail's flow with your spirit sense
choices.text: You trace the thread of qi through each lantern and find where it all drains. You redirect it, and the nearest lanterns brighten into a clean guiding light.

on_fail.text: The thread slips through your sense and every lantern goes out at once. You grope back through the dark with only a little qi gathered.

choices.label: Leave the lanterns alone
choices.text: Not every light in the mist is meant for you. You turn back, and the lanterns burn on behind you.

encounters.name: The Thunder-Struck Oak
encounters.text: A great oak split by heavenly lightning stands blackened in a clearing, its heartwood still crackling with violet sparks long after the storm. Hunters say the tree remembers the Tribulation that struck it.

choices.label: Sit beneath it and temper your meridians
choices.text: Sparks stitch along your arms as you breathe with the crackling. It hurts exactly as much as a cleansing should, and you rise lighter and sharper.

choices.label: Cut a sliver of the heartwood
choices.text: The saw rings and sparks, but a palm-wide sliver comes free. A talisman maker in the market will pay well for it.
