choices.label: Burn the oak down for the sparks
choices.text: Thunder-fire catches, and the clearing roars. You sift a few stones' worth of charged ash from the cinders, and the forest does not forget the smell.

encounters.name: The Veiled Appraiser
encounters.text: A veiled woman sits behind a table bare but for a brass scale and a jade tray. "Foundation Establishment is when buyers stop haggling over your face and begin pricing your future," she says. "Let me weigh yours, for a small fee."

choices.label: Pay 20 spirit stones for the weighing
choices.text: She tilts the scale and names three flaws in your breathing you had not noticed. Correcting them takes the rest of the day and is worth more than the fee.

choices.label: Haggle her down
choices.text: Half an hour of friendly argument later she waves you off with a small advice and no fee. You do not mind.

on_fail.text: She names a price twice the first and turns back to her scale. You walk on poorer in patience, not in stones.

choices.label: Slip a stone from her jade tray
choices.text: She does not look up. "Weighed," she says softly, and the stone is cold in your sleeve. Her veil turns to follow you out of the market.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.text: She nods as if you had answered a question. "Few do. Come back when the price of your future has risen." You do not.

encounters.name: Crumbs of the Pill Auction
encounters.text: The back hall of an auction house is being swept after a sale of rare pills. Dust of crushed medicine lies thick in the corners, and the sweeping boy eyes the broom, then the hall's guards, then you.

choices.label: Pay the boy a few stones to sweep the dust into a pouch
choices.text: You settle with him and sift the pill dust at your lodgings. Most of it is chaff, but a pinch still rings with medicine qi.

choices.label: Sweep alongside him for the house
choices.text: The steward watches you work, then tips the boy and you each a small purse. Honest labour is not unheard of at Foundation.

choices.label: Pocket a loose pill from the porters' crate
choices.text: A cracked pill lies in the straw. You have it away before the guard turns, and it will fetch a good price in some other market.

encounters.name: Hands for the Planting
encounters.text: The thaw has come and {villager}'s family is racing the rains to get the rice seedlings into the paddy, bent double in the cold mud. One more pair of hands would save a day's work.

choices.label: Wade in and plant beside them
choices.text: You roll your sleeves and work the rows until dusk, qi steadying your back where theirs would ache. {villager} sends you home with a bundle of the first tender greens.

choices.label: Stir the paddy water with a thread of qi
choices.text: A little qi through the water warms the seedbed and loosens the mud. The rows go in twice as fast and the family bows you off, a touch in awe.

choices.label: Wish them luck and walk on
choices.text: Planting is no work for a cultivator. You nod to {villager} and go your way.

encounters.name: The Flooded Field
encounters.text: A summer storm has stood over the valley since dawn, and the stream has burst its bank into {villager}'s lowest field. Half the barley is under brown water, and neighbours are shouting over a shovel and a few sandbags.

choices.label: Dig the channel with them
choices.text: You work the drain till your hands blister, and the water bleeds away toward the stream. Most of the barley is saved. {villager} presses a pouch of coppers and herbs on you, though you try to refuse.

choices.label: Turn the stream aside with a burst of qi
choices.text: A sweep of your palm, a mound of earth rising where it should, and the stream shrugs and finds its old bed. The farmers fall silent, then bow.

choices.label: Wait out the storm under the eaves
choices.text: The rain eases by evening. What can be saved has been saved, and you were not part of it.

encounters.name: The Autumn Hunt Drive
encounters.text: Boar have been raiding the ripe fields, and the village hunters are forming a drive through the wood, banging pots and gongs. {villager}, bow in hand, asks if you will walk the line and watch for anything bigger than a boar.

choices.label: Walk the line with the hunters
choices.text: You hold the flank through two long days of shouting and leaf-fall. Nothing worse than boar breaks cover, and the hunters share the haunch and a good deal of wine.

choices.label: Take the best spot to meet what flees
choices.text: You settle where the game will run, and take the share of the hunt that the heavens send you. The hunters grumble, but the meat is good.

choices.label: Decline; hunting is for hunters
choices.text: You watch the line vanish into the colour of the trees.

encounters.name: A Traveller in the Snow
encounters.text: A peddler sits in the snow beside the road, grey-lipped, his mule dead in the traces. His hands will not close on his pack. He has perhaps an hour of life in him.

choices.label: Warm him with your qi and carry him to shelter
choices.text: You press your palms to his back until blood returns to his fingers, then carry him to a hearth in the village. He weeps, and promises to name your kindness in every market he reaches.

choices.label: Give him your cloak and send him to the village
choices.text: He stammers thanks and limps down the road in your cloak. It will be a cold walk, but a short one.

choices.label: Take the pack and walk on
choices.text: The snow will cover him soon enough. His pack holds a few stones and a roll of tea.

encounters.name: A Patch in the Fog
encounters.text: The fog has swallowed the path, and you follow the sound of dripping water instead. It leads you down a hollow where a glimmer of pale leaves shows through the grey, a herb patch no gatherer has marked.

choices.label: Harvest carefully, leaving the roots
choices.text: You cut only the outer leaves and tuck the earth back around the roots, as the old gatherers taught. The patch will return next year.

choices.label: Strip the whole patch
choices.text: You take every leaf and every root. When the fog lifts, only trampled earth remains.

choices.label: Mark the way and leave it
choices.text: You tie a rag to a branch and walk back the way the water ran. Some secrets are better kept for the forest.

encounters.name: Meteors Over the Market
encounters.text: A night of cloudless black, and the old stargazers on the market wall say the sky will burn tonight. Lanterns are hushed. You sit among cultivators and tradesmen with your face tipped to the dark, and the first streak crosses the heavens.

choices.label: Open your senses to the falling stars
choices.text: Each streak leaves a thin wake of qi in the cold air. You breathe it in until dawn, and your dantian hums with borrowed starlight.

choices.label: Share a jug of wine with the stargazers
choices.text: The old men tell you the names of the stars and what each omen means for the harvest. You leave with a headache and a good tale, and a stranger's coin pressed in your hand.

encounters.name: The Flock Under the Ledge
encounters.text: Thunder walks the hills, and the rain comes sideways. Under a rocky ledge above the village, {villager} crouches among a huddle of bleating sheep, one arm around a lamb, shouting after the half of the flock still lost in the dark.

choices.label: Search the slope and bring the strays in
choices.text: You wade the streaming gullies by lightning-flash and carry the stragglers back one by one. By dawn the count is whole, and {villager} will not stop thanking you.

choices.label: Hold the ledge and calm the flock
choices.text: You sit among the sheep and let a little warm qi settle them while the storm passes. Not all are saved, but most are, and {villager} presses a few coins on you.

choices.label: Leave them to the storm
choices.text: It is not your flock. You walk on through the rain with your collar up.

encounters.name: The Tree the Lightning Took
encounters.text: A bolt has just split an old pine from crown to root, and the smell of scorched air hangs about it. Along the open heartwood a faint violet glimmer still crawls, as if the lightning had left a word behind.

choices.label: Sit by the split trunk and read the residue
choices.text: You steady your breath and follow the glimmer's rhythm, its sudden bright strokes and long hush. For a moment you hear the thunder as speech. Then the trace gutters out, and something of it stays with you.

choices.label: Chip a splinter of the charred wood
choices.text: A palm-length sliver of lightning-struck wood comes away warm in your hand.

choices.label: Leave it and find shelter
choices.text: The next bolt lands closer. You do not argue with the sky.

encounters.name: The Peddler With the Broken Wheel
encounters.text: A peddler's cart sits tilted in the roadside mud, one wheel cracked through, his bundles of dried herbs sagging under a leaking tarp. The rain hammers on it. He looks at you, then at the wheel, and does not ask.

choices.label: Heave the cart clear while he swaps the wheel
choices.text: You get your shoulder under the axle and heave it clear of the mud while he hammers the spare on. He grins through the rain and swears you will get his best price at the herb stall for a month.

choices.label: Pay five stones for a wheelwright's help
choices.text: The wheelwright is fetched, the wheel is mended, and the peddler counts your stones twice, gratefully. He promises you a fair price at the herb stall for a month.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: He watches you go. The rain does not care either.
